author: tarik37
body:
### Motivation

- Fournir une extension Chrome pour transcrire les vidéos et lives TikTok en affichant une overlay de transcription, en privilégiant les légendes natives si présentes et en lançant un ASR local sinon.
- Éviter les téléchargements répétés du modèle en conservant le modèle Whisper v3 Turbo en cache navigateur / IndexedDB pour réutilisation ultérieure.

### Description

- Ajout de `manifest.json` avec permissions `tabCapture`, `offscreen` et `storage` et wiring d’un service worker `background.js`.
- Ajout d’un script de contenu `content.js` qui crée un bandeau d’overlay, détecte les légendes via plusieurs sélecteurs et bascule en mode hybride entre `captions` et `asr` avec boutons `Start`/`Stop`.
- Ajout d’une orchestration background + offscreen via `background.js` et `offscreen.html`/`offscreen.js` qui créent un document offscreen (`chrome.offscreen.createDocument`) et obtiennent un `streamId` via `chrome.tabCapture.getMediaStreamId`, puis enregistrent l’audio par `MediaRecorder` et envoient des chunks au worker.
- Ajout de `worker-asr.js` qui importe `@xenova/transformers` et initialise un pipeline `automatic-speech-recognition` pour `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` (avec `env.useBrowserCache = true`) et émet des messages `ASR_STATUS` et `TRANSCRIPT_PARTIAL` vers le content script; le worker gère l’initialisation du modèle, la transcription de chunks et le nettoyage de session.
- Mise à jour de `README.md` avec instructions d’installation locale et limitations connues (sélecteurs DOM TikTok, dépendances WebGPU / permissions).

### Testing

- Validation JSON du manifest exécutée avec `python -m json.tool manifest.json` et passée avec succès.
- Vérification de la syntaxe JavaScript exécutée avec `node --check` sur `background.js`, `offscreen.js`, `content.js` et `worker-asr.js`, et toutes les vérifications sont passées.

author: co-esquie
body:
After reviewing https://github.com/ericcurtin/inferrs/pull/157, Fixes a crash when loading Qwen3.5 models by refactoring `VisionConfig` from a single flat struct into an enum with per-family variants (`Gemma4` / `Qwen`), enabling proper support for Qwen3.5's different vision encoder config shape.

### Problem

On `main`, loading a Qwen3.5 model would crash because `vision_config` in Qwen3.5's `config.json` has a completely different schema than Gemma4's (e.g. `depth` instead of `num_hidden_layers`, no `pooling_kernel_size`, etc.). The single `VisionConfig` struct couldn't deserialize it.

**Broken on `main`:**
```bash
./target/release/inferrs run Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B "Describe docker company in one sentence" --device=cuda
```

author: copilot
body:
The Main Overlay Score Duels page (Page 5) allowed starting a search without the same prerequisite validation enforced by the GUI tab. It also lacked inline duel rules.

### Changes

- **New `_overlay_page6_check_prerequisites()` helper** — shared by both HTML builder and search action. Returns `""` on success or the first failing lock message, evaluated in priority order:
  1. Player Name set (not default `"Player"`)
  2. Cloud Sync enabled + `CLOUD_URL` configured
  3. VPS-ID assignments > 0
  4. Available Maps cache non-empty

- **IDLE state HTML** — adds two duel rule lines before the action hint, and conditionally renders either `◀ Start Search` or the lock message in `#FF3B30`:

```
⚠️ One game only — restarting in-game will abort the duel!
🔙 After the duel, close VPX or return to Popper.

🔒 Player Name not set – set in System tab   ← shown instead of Start Search
```

- **`_overlay_page6_start_search()` guard** — calls the same helper before `join_matchmaking()`, shows mini info message and returns early on failure

- **Removed redundant bottom warning** — the `⚠️ One game only per duel` line appended to all states (IDLE/SEARCHING/MATCH_FOUND) is removed; rules are now inline where appropriate

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Main Overlay Auto-Match: Add duel rules + 4 prerequisite checks (same as GUI)

### Summary

The Main Overlay Page 5 (Score Duels Auto-Match) IDLE state needs two changes:

1. **Show the duel rules** before the Start Search button
2. **Same 4 prerequisite checks as the GUI** — if any check fails, show a lock message instead of `◀ Start Search`, and block ← Left from starting the search

### 1. Duel rules on IDLE page

In `ui/overlay_pages.py` → `_overlay_page6_build_html()`, in the `state == "IDLE"` block, add these two lines **before** the `◀ Start Search` action hint:

```
⚠️ One game only — restarting in-game will abort the duel!
🔙 After the duel, close VPX or return to Popper.
```

The IDLE page should look like this:

```
⚔️ Score Duels
─────────────────────────

🔍 Auto-Match
Find an opponent on a shared table automatically.

⚠️ One game only — restarting in-game will abort the duel!
🔙 After the duel, close VPX or return to Popper.

◀ Start Search

Use your configured Left / Right keys from Tab Controls to navigate.
```

**Important:** Remove the bottom warning line `⚠️ One game only per duel — restarting (F3) will abort the duel! (NVRAM tracking)` that is currently appended at the very end of ALL states (IDLE, SEARCHING, MATCH_FOUND) in `_overlay_page6_build_html()` around line 956-958. The rules are now shown inline in each state where appropriate, so this redundant bottom warning is no longer needed.

### 2. Four prerequisite checks

The same 4 checks from `ui/duels.py` → `_update_duel_cloud_overlays()` (lines 630-678) must be replicated. The checks are evaluated **in priority order** — show the first failing check:

| Priority | Check | Lock message |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Player Name set and not "Player" | `🔒 Player Name not set – set in System tab` |
| 2 | Cloud Sync enabled + CLOUD_URL set | `🔒 Cloud Sync required – enable in System tab` |
| 3 | VPS-ID assignments > 0 | `🔒 No VPS-IDs assigned – assign in Available Maps tab` |
| 4 | Available Maps loaded (non-empty list) | `🔒 Available Maps not loaded – load maps first` |

#### In `_overlay_page6_build_html()` IDLE state:

- Run the 4 checks
- If **all pass**: show `◀ Start Search` as the action hint (current behavior)
- If **any fails**: show the lock message (e.g. `🔒 Player Name not set – set in System tab`) **instead of** `◀ Start Search` — in a warning/lock color like `#FF3B30` or `#FFAA00`

#### In `_overlay_page6_start_search()`:

- Add the same 4 checks as guards **before** calling `join_matchmaking()`
- If any check fails, show a mini info message (`_on_mini_info_message()`) with the lock message and return early
- This prevents ← Left from starting the search even if the HTML somehow doesn't block it

#### How to implement the checks:

```python
# Check 1: Player Name
pname = str(self.cfg.OVERLAY.get("player_name", "Player") or "").strip()
check1_ok = bool(pname and pname.lower() != "player")

# Check 2: Cloud Sync
cloud_ok = bool(
    getattr(self.cfg, "CLOUD_ENABLED", False)
    and str(getattr(self.cfg, "CLOUD_URL", "") or "").strip()
)

# Check 3: VPS-IDs
try:
    from ui.vps import _load_vps_mapping
    vps_count = len(_load_vps_mapping(self.cfg))
except Exception:
    vps_count = 0
check3_ok = vps_count > 0

# Check 4: Available Maps

# PR: Timeline Legend in Header Component

## Summary

This PR adds the timeline legend to the right side of `Header.razor`, completing the header's visual layout per `OriginalDesignConcept.html`. The legend displays four symbol-label pairs in a horizontal flexbox row with 22px gap: PoC Milestone (gold diamond), Production Release (green diamond), Checkpoint (gray circle), and Now line (red vertical bar with dynamic "Now ({Month} {Year})" label derived from `data.json` timeline dates). The legend is positioned via the existing parent `.hdr` flexbox `space-between` layout established in the prior Header PR (#571). This PR **only modifies** `src/ReportingDashboard/Components/Header.razor`.

**Source Issue:** #572
**Depends On:** #570 (Foundation), #571 (Header & Metadata)
**Parent Issue:** #560

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Legend Container
- [ ] A `<div>` with `display: flex; gap: 22px; align-items: center` renders on the right side of the `.hdr` div, positioned by the parent flexbox `justify-content: space-between`.
- [ ] The legend container sits at the same vertical center as the title/subtitle block.

### PoC Milestone Symbol
- [ ] A `<span>` renders as a 12×12px square with `background: #F4B400` and `transform: rotate(45deg)` to form a diamond shape.
- [ ] Adjacent 12px label text reads **"PoC Milestone"**.

### Production Release Symbol
- [ ] A `<span>` renders as a 12×12px square with `background: #34A853` and `transform: rotate(45deg)` to form a diamond shape.
- [ ] Adjacent 12px label text reads **"Production Release"**.

### Checkpoint Symbol
- [ ] A `<span>` renders as an 8×8px circle with `border-radius: 50%` and `background: #999`.
- [ ] Adjacent 12px label text reads **"Checkpoint"**.

### Now Line Symbol
- [ ] A `<span>` renders as a 2×14px vertical bar with `background: #EA4335`.
- [ ] Adjacent 12px label text reads **"Now ({Month} {Year})"** where `{Month}` and `{Year}` are dynamically derived from `Data.Timeline.NowDate`.
- [ ] If `NowDate` cannot be parsed, the label falls back to **"Now ({CurrentMonth})"** using `Data.CurrentMonth`.

### Visual Fidelity
- [ ] All four legend items render inline in a single horizontal row.
- [ ] Symbol shapes visually match the corresponding markers in the SVG timeline (diamonds for PoC/Production, circle for checkpoint, vertical bar for NOW line).
- [ ] Legend label font is 12px, weight 400, inheriting the base font family (`Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif`).
- [ ] Side-by-side comparison with `OriginalDesignConcept.html` header section shows visual parity.

### Build
- [ ] `dotnet build` succeeds with zero errors after changes.

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Add legend container div and symbol-label structure

Inside `Header.razor`, add a new `<div>` to the right side of the existing `.hdr` flexbox container. This div uses inline styles `display: flex; gap: 22px; align-items: center` (or a CSS class if one exists in `dashboard.css`). Inside it, create four child elements — each a `<span>` wrapper containing a symbol `<span>` and a label `<span>`. Use inline styles on each symbol span to set dimensions, background color, and shape transforms:

- PoC: `width: 12px; height: 12px; background: #F4B400; transform: rotate(45deg); display: inline-block`
- Production: `width: 12px; height: 12px; background: #34A853; transform: rotate(45deg); display: inline-block`
- Checkpoint: `width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: #999; display: inline-block`
- Now: `width: 2px; height: 14px; background: #EA4335; display: inline-block`

Each label span uses `font-size: 12px; margin-left: 6px`. Hardcode all four labels with static text for now (use placeholder "Now" for the fourth item).

**Commit:** `feat: add legend container with four symbol-label pairs to Header`

### Step 2: Implement dynamic Now label from timeline NowDate

Add a private computed property `NowLabel` in the `@code` block that:
1. Attempts to parse `Data.Timeline.NowDate` as a `DateTime`.
2. On success, formats it as `"Now ({Month:MMMM} {Year:yyyy})"` — e.g., `"Now (April 2026)"`.
3. On failure (empty string or invalid date), falls back to `$"Now ({Data.CurrentMonth})"`.

Replace the hardcoded "Now" label text with `@NowLabel`. Add a null guard so that if `Data` or `Data.Timeline` is null, the label defaults to `"Now"`.

**Commit:** `feat: derive Now legend label dynamically from timeline NowDate`

### Step 3: Polish alignment and verify against OriginalDesignConcept.html

Fine-tune vertical alignment of diamond shapes (rotated squares may need a margin adjustment or wrapper with `overflow: visible` to prevent clipping). Ensure each legend item wrapper uses `display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px` for consistent symbol-to-label spacing. Verify that the legend renders identically to the reference HTML by visual comparison. Confirm `dotnet build` succeeds with zero errors.

**Commit:** `fix: polish legend alignment and verify visual fidelity`

---

## Testing

### Unit Tests (bUnit — `tests/ReportingDashboard.Tests/Unit/Components/`)

Extend or add tests in the existing `HeaderTests.cs` or `HeaderInlineTests.cs`:

- **Legend renders four items** — Render `Header` with valid `DashboardData`; assert the legend container contains exactly 4 symbol-label groups.
- **PoC diamond symbol** — Assert a `<span>` exists with inline style containing `#F4B400` and `rotate(45deg)`, with adjacent text "PoC Milestone".
- **Production diamond symbol** — Assert a `<span>` exists with inline style containing `#34A853` and `rotate(45deg)`, with adjacent text "Production Release".
- **Checkpoint circle symbol** — Assert a `<span>` exists with inline style containing `border-radius` and `#999`, with adjacent text "Checkpoint".
- **Now bar symbol** — Assert a `<span>` exists with inline style containing `#EA4335`, with adjacent text matching the dynamic Now label.
- **Now label from valid NowDate** — Set `Timeline.NowDate = "2026-04-10"`, assert legend text contains `"Now (April 2026)"`.
- **Now label fallback on empty NowDate** — Set `Timeline.NowDate = ""` and `CurrentMonth = "Apr"`, assert legend text contains `"Now (Apr)"`.
- **Now label fallback on invalid NowDate** — Set `Timeline.NowDate = "not-a-date"` and `CurrentMonth = "Mar"`, assert legend text contains `"Now (Mar)"`.
- **Legend gap spacing** — Assert the legend container has `gap: 22px` in its style attribute or CSS class.

### Build Verification
- `dotnet build` passes with zero errors.
- `dotnet test` passes for all existing + new header tests.

### Visual Verification (Manual)
- Run `dotnet run`, open `http://localhost:5000`, compare header legend against `OriginalDesignConcept.html` side-by-side.
- Confirm diamond shapes are visually identical to SVG timeline diamonds.
- Confirm the Now label updates when `data.json` `timeline.nowDate` is changed and the app is restarted.

body:
## Summary

Pure refactor. \`src/App.jsx\` had grown to 1078 lines / ~13k tokens — over the 10k-token Read file limit, so reading the file for any future edit fails with a \"File content exceeds maximum allowed tokens\" error. Extracted three custom hooks so the root component fits in a single read.

**Zero behaviour changes.** Every effect, callback, state initializer, and dependency array moved mechanically — the state tree is identical, just rehoused.

## Extracted hooks (all under \`src/hooks/\`)

### \`useStockScan.js\`
Owns the single-stock scan pipeline:
- \`runScan\` with the Zerodha → Dhan → Yahoo fallback chain and token-expiry detection
- \`candles\` / \`patterns\` / \`box\` / \`risk\` state + the engine-specific detector/scorer dispatch (scalp variants / classic / intraday)
- Fire-and-forget news fetch with the \`stockNewsReqIdRef\` stale-response guard
- Yahoo bid/ask quote fetching effect
- Timeframe-triggered re-scan
- Lazy left-edge history prefetch (\`handleLoadMoreHistory\`)
- Persistent recent-history list

Takes engine config + dataSource state in; emits an \`onDiscoverSymbol\` callback so App can grow the broad autocomplete universe with newly-scanned symbols.

### \`useIndexUniverse.js\`
Owns the index / symbol universe:
- \`nseIndex\` selection with localStorage persistence
- Constituent fetching + sessionStorage cache (\`readNseSymsCache\` / \`writeNseSymsCache\`)
- Broad NIFTY TOTAL MARKET prefetch for autocomplete
- Custom indices add/remove
- Dynamic-index auto-refresh (Top Gainers / Losers, 30s interval)
- A \`refreshIndex\` callback that bumps the refresh key

### \`useAppView.js\`
Owns top-level view routing:
- \`view\` state ('main' / 'batch' / 'simulate' / 'paper' / 'novice' / 'settings')
- \`setView\` with \`pushState\` bookkeeping
- popstate handler with double-back-to-exit (2s window) and Zerodha-OAuth-return landing
- \`cameFromBatch\` / \`cameFromSimulation\` / \`settingsReturnView\` flags

## Before / after

| | \`src/App.jsx\` |
|---|---|
| Before | 1078 lines, ~13k tokens (unreadable in one call) |
| After  | 604 lines, fits in one Read |

Extracted lines live in 3 new files:
- \`src/hooks/useStockScan.js\` — 352 lines
- \`src/hooks/useIndexUniverse.js\` — 181 lines
- \`src/hooks/useAppView.js\` — 72 lines

## Things I was careful about

- \`history\` (recent scans) moved *into* \`useStockScan\` along with its localStorage-persist effect, because the scan is what appends to it. App still destructures \`history, setHistory\` from the hook for the Recent pills in the JSX.
- \`broadSearchSymbols\` / \`broadCompanyMap\` stay in \`useIndexUniverse\` (where they're seeded from NIFTY TOTAL MARKET). \`useStockScan\` doesn't own them — instead it accepts an \`onDiscoverSymbol\` callback that App wires into the universe setters. This avoids duplicated state between the two hooks.
- \`activeFilters\` stays in App.jsx because its initializer depends on \`engineVersion\` and the engineVersion-change effect needs to call its setter — moving both would require one hook to know about the other.
- The \`useEffect\` that re-syncs \`dataSource\` from localStorage on return to main view stays in App.jsx because it reaches into \`setTimeframe\` which also lives in App. Keeping it here avoids needing to pass the timeframe setter through a hook boundary for one effect.
- \`useRef\` for \`chartRef\` stays in App.jsx — it's rendered prop drilling, not state.

## Test plan

- [x] 178/178 unit tests passing (unchanged from pre-refactor)
- [x] \`npm run build\` clean, 130.09 KB gzipped (was 129.39 — +0.7 KB from a trivial amount of hook-boundary duplication, acceptable)
- [x] \`src/App.jsx\` now reads in one Read call without the token-limit error
- [ ] Browser smoke test: load the app, verify each view (Stock / Index / Simulation / Paper Trading / Novice / Settings) still routes correctly
- [ ] Scan a stock, verify candles + patterns + risk + news all populate as before
- [ ] Switch dataSource to Zerodha in Settings → scan with an expired token → verify the fallback-to-Yahoo banner still fires
- [ ] Scroll the chart left edge on a Yahoo scan → verify the lazy history prefetch still prepends candles without losing scroll position
- [ ] Back button behavior: from Batch → back → main; from main → back twice → exit PWA

No strategy / engine / simulation code was touched. The 17-day baseline is unaffected.

author: debaerdm
body:
Add a Claude Code skill at `.claude/skills/issue-to-pr/SKILL.md` that captures the full workflow for resolving a GitHub issue in this monorepo end-to-end: from reading the issue to opening a labeled PR.

## What it does

Guides Claude Code through 7 phases when a user asks it to work on an issue:

1. **Safety triage** — mandatory first check because the repo is public. Stops and asks the user before touching anything auth / CSP / crypto / secrets / PII / CI-CD / security-labelled.
2. **Anti-duplicate check** — searches open/closed/merged PRs for the issue number before starting, so we don't redo work where someone forgot to close the issue.
3. **Understand the issue** — theme scope, component, change type, acceptance criteria. Asks if ambiguous.
4. **Locate files** — encodes the filename-based scope rules from [.github/git-commit-instructions.md](.github/git-commit-instructions.md) (`*Apollo` → prospect, `*LF` → client, `*Common` → both, etc.) so the commit scope is picked correctly every time.
5. **Edit minimally** — surgical changes only, with a worked example of preserving the untouched breakpoint when an issue scopes a change to mobile only.
6. **Visual verification** — launches Storybook on a free port with `--ci --no-open` to avoid the silent-hang pitfall when the default port (6410) is already taken. Waits for the user to confirm the pixel before committing.
7. **Commit / push / PR / labels** — enforces conventional commit format, branch naming, short PR body with `Closes #N`, and label inheritance from the issue + `css-package` / `react-package` based on touched paths.

Three explicit confirmation gates stop Claude from silently running shared-state actions (visual tests on sensitive issues, push, PR creation).

## Why

Complements the existing GitHub Copilot setup under [.github/agents/](.github/agents/) and [.github/skills/](.github/skills/) with an equivalent for Claude Code users on the team. Nothing in the existing Copilot/CI tooling changes.

## Scope

Only adds one file. No code / CSS / config touched.

body:
[ 왜 바꿨는가? ] 
- LLM이 mission/scene 정보를 바탕으로 오프닝에서 상대의 의도나 다음 행동을 추론해 먼저 언급하거나, 상대의 선택/행동을 주어로 삼아 발화하는 경우가 반복적으로 발생
- 자연스러운 자기 감각·관찰·인사 중심의 첫 마디를 유도하고, mission/scene의 논리적 일관성 및 표현 방식 일치를 보장하기 위해 프롬프트와 예시, constraint를 명확히 기술
- 테스트 코드 보강을 통해 새로운 프롬프트/로직이 의도대로 동작하는지 검증


[ 핵심 구조 변화 ] 
scene은 각 페르소나별로 2문장:
1문장: 자기 정보(행동·소지품·신체 상태, 주어=자기)
2문장: 상대 정보(행동·소지품·신체 상태, 주어=상대)
→ mission 의도 직접 언급 금지, 논리적 충돌 방지


[ 세부 파일 변경 내용 ]
1. base_chat.py
 - 프롬프트 버전 관리 주석 보강 및 중복 선언 정리
 - SYSTEM_PROMPT 내 역할 안내 강화:
 - “상대의 상황에서 너의 name(이름) 또는 role(역할)이 주어로 등장하는 정보를 우선하여 너의 행동과 상태를 파악하라.”
 → 페르소나 주어 명확화, 자연스러운 행동·반응 유도

2. opening.py
 - 오프닝 프롬프트 가이드라인 강화 및 예시 보강
 - 1번: “반드시 너(AI) 자신의 짧은 인사, 상태·감각, 눈앞의 관찰 중 하나로 시작해라”로 명확화, 
 -   “상대를 주어로 한 행동·시선·선택·소지품 묘사로 첫 화제를 시작하지 마라” 추가
 - 5번: user_scene 기반 추론 및 선제적 반응 금지 내용을 분리·강조
 - Bad 예시에 “떡볶이 맛있어 보여요?” 추가

3. scenario.py
 - SYSTEM_PROMPT 내 scene 작성 규칙을 명확히 2문장 구조로 고정
 - mission 의도 직접 언급 금지, 행동·상태로만 암시
 - 각 문장 속 행동이 mission과 논리적으로 충돌하지 않아야 함
 - 주석/예시/테스트 모두 이 구조에 맞게 보강

4. generate_scenario.py
 - 실행 예시에서 --with-opening → --with_opening 오타 수정

5. test_ai_response_node.py
 - 테스트용 state의 scene 예시를 2문장 구조(“두 사람은 처음 보는 사이입니다. ...”)로 수정

6. test_generate_openings_node.py
 - 테스트용 persona의 scene을 2문장 구조로 수정하여 opening 생성 로직 검증 강화

7. test_generate_scenario_node.py
  - SYSTEM_PROMPT/USER_PROMPT에 이번에 변경한 프롬프트 수정 사항이 잘 포함되는지 검증 코드 보강

8. test_opening_helpers.py
 - mission/scene 예시를 최신 규칙(행동형 mission, 2문장 scene)으로 수정



[ 기대 효과 ]
 - 오프닝/시나리오에서 mission/scene 정보가 과도하게 반영되어 발생하는 부자연스러운 첫 마디 및 논리적 충돌 방지
 - LLM이 상황에 맞는 자연스러운 첫 인사·관찰·감각 중심의 발화를 생성하도록 유도
 - 시나리오/오프닝 품질 및 논리적 일관성 향상, 테스트 신뢰도 제고

We intentionally keep tutorial scripts non-optimal for learning purposes, but they should at least be bug-free. Currently, the script for buying cloud servers is somewhat buggy; while it works fine on the first run, it crashes with `scp: Invalid host: '' (empty string)` if the player already owns servers.

While experienced players can easily fix this, it can be a major roadblock for new players with limited programming experience. This PR updates the script to work properly even when the player reruns it.

The updated script still fits within the basic 8GB home RAM limit, so RAM usage is not a problem.

body:
## 背景

データセットと学習済みモデルがリポジトリ内に混在しており、今後ファイル数が数万規模に拡大する見込み・複数PC間での実験運用を考えると構成上の負担が大きい。コードとデータを分離し、リポジトリ外（`../ml-data/graph-convnet-uelb/`）で管理する形に変更する。

## 変更内容

### 追加
- `src/common/config/paths.py`: データ/モデルのパス解決ヘルパー
  - 優先順位: 環境変数 (`GCN_UELB_DATA_ROOT` / `GCN_UELB_MODEL_ROOT`) → config の `data_root` / `model_root` → デフォルト (`<Projects>/ml-data/graph-convnet-uelb/`)
  - データセット名は config の `dataset_name` → `expt_name` にフォールバック
  - 提供関数: `get_data_root`, `get_model_root`, `get_dataset_dir`, `get_mode_dir`, `get_graph_file`, `get_commodity_file`, `get_node_flow_file`, `get_exact_solution_file`, `dataset_exists`

### コード更新 (パスヘルパー経由に統一)
- `src/common/data_management/` — `DatasetReader` に `config` 引数を追加、`create_data_files` / `dataset_manager` でハードコードパスを除去
- `src/gcn/train/` — `trainer` / `evaluator`
- `src/gcn/algorithms/` — `algorithm_examples` / `beamsearch_comparator`
- `src/rl_ksp/` — `environment/rl_environment` / `train/rl_trainer`
- `src/seq_flow_rl/training/trainer`
- `scripts/`: `generate_data`, `train_gcn`, `train_rl_ksp`, `train_seqflowrl`, `tune_hyperparameters`, `two_phase_training` の存在チェックを共通の `dataset_exists()` に統一

### Config クリーンアップ
- 18 個の JSON から不要になった `models_dir: "./saved_models"` と `checkpoint_dir: "saved_models/seqflowrl/"` を削除

## ディレクトリ構造

```
<Projects>/
├── graph-convnet-uelb/        # このリポジトリ

    │       ├── train_data/
    │       ├── val_data/

```bash

# 2. 任意の位置を使う場合は環境変数で指定

export GCN_UELB_MODEL_ROOT=/path/to/saved_models
```

author: kaden-schutt
body:
## Summary
- `hipfire update` ran a plain `git pull origin master` that aborted with `Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge` whenever a tracked file was modified (most commonly `Cargo.lock`, which `cargo build` rewrites when the lockfile format version diverges from the committed one). The exit code wasn't checked, so the update then silently rebuilt from stale code.
- Replace with: `fetch` → refuse on feature branches / unpushed commits → stash dirty tree as `hipfire-update-<ISO ts>` (recoverable via `git stash pop`) → `git reset --hard origin/master`. Every step has explicit exit-code checks via a `must()` helper.
- `scripts/install.sh` gets the same treatment on its existing-clone path. The old interactive prompt defaulted to `N`, so non-interactive `curl|bash` runs silently left stale checkouts; the new flow unconditionally stashes (as `hipfire-install-<ts>`), fetches, and hard-resets.

## Reported error (verbatim)
```
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
        Cargo.lock
        Cargo.toml
Please commit your changes or stash them before you merge.
Aborting
```

## Behavior matrix
| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clean tree | `git pull` (works) | `fetch` + `reset --hard` (works, no stash) |
| Dirty tree (the bug) | `git pull` aborts, rebuild uses stale code | Stash + hard-reset; user recovers via `git stash pop` |
| Feature branch | `git pull origin master` does weird things | Refuse with clear message (rc=1) |
| Unpushed commits on master | `git pull` would merge, but still broken if tree dirty | Refuse with clear message (rc=1); commits untouched |
| Diverged history | `git pull` creates merge commits | Hard-reset to origin/master (consistent) |
| Shallow clone | Worked | Still works (fetch extends depth) |

## Test plan
`scripts/tests/test-update-dirty-tree.sh` (new, 221 lines) is self-contained and runs in a `mktemp -d`:
- [x] Baseline reproduction: asserts plain `git pull origin master` still fails with the exact reported error message
- [x] Dirty-tree happy path: tree ends at upstream HEAD, clean, stash preserved with `hipfire-update-` marker
- [x] Clean-tree no-op: updates successfully with no stash created
- [x] Feature-branch guard: returns rc=10
- [x] Unpushed-commits guard: returns rc=11; local commit intact after refusal
- [x] Divergence guard: greps `cli/index.ts` for the required markers and forbids the old `"pull", "origin", "master"` call from returning
- [x] Red-green verified: reverting `cli/index.ts` to master makes the test fail, restoring makes it pass

Also verified:
- `bash -n scripts/install.sh` — syntax OK

body:
## Summary

Final fix for `test_exact_path_in_list_allowed` which failed on Windows/macOS.

**Root cause**: Using a single *file* path (e.g. `/tmp/dcc_mcp_test_file.py`) as the allowed path fails when the file doesn't exist — `canonicalize()` returns the raw path without resolving symlinks, so the prefix-match in `check_path()` fails.

**Fix**: Allow the parent **directory** (`tempfile.gettempdir()`, which always exists) and verify a child file is permitted. This correctly resolves macOS `/tmp → /private/tmp` and Windows `%TEMP%` paths.

## Test plan

- [x] Ubuntu: passes (child file allowed under tmp dir)  
- [x] macOS: passes (resolves `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` correctly)  
- [x] Windows: passes (uses actual `%TEMP%` directory)

author: ryanbr
body:
## Summary
Adds \`#EXT-X-PRELOAD-HINT\` to the lines stripped during ad blocking, alongside the existing \`#EXT-X-TWITCH-PREFETCH\` removal. Ports TTV-AB 6.1.9 (commit a81ac73 — 'fix(playback): harden prefetch ad stripping').

## Why
vaft and video-swap-new already strip the Twitch-proprietary \`#EXT-X-TWITCH-PREFETCH\` lines from m3u8 playlists during ad blocking, to prevent the low-latency prefetch path from leaking ad segments into playback. The HLS standard equivalent is \`#EXT-X-PRELOAD-HINT\`. If Twitch transitions to the standard tag (which they may, given they're moving toward standard LL-HLS), the existing strip would miss it and ad media could be prefetched.

This is a forward-compatibility hardening — it costs nothing if the tag isn't present, and protects against the case where it appears.

## Change
One-line addition in all four release files:

\`\`\`diff
- if (lines[i].startsWith('#EXT-X-TWITCH-PREFETCH:')) {
+ if (lines[i].startsWith('#EXT-X-TWITCH-PREFETCH:') || lines[i].startsWith('#EXT-X-PRELOAD-HINT:')) {
      lines[i] = '';
  }
\`\`\`

Files touched:
- \`vaft/vaft.user.js\`
- \`vaft/vaft-ublock-origin.js\`
- \`video-swap-new/video-swap-new.user.js\`
- \`video-swap-new/video-swap-new-ublock-origin.js\`

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify normal playback isn't affected
- [ ] Watch debug logs for any \`EXT-X-PRELOAD-HINT\` references during ad breaks (currently rare on Twitch but worth observing)

## Risk
Minimal. The change only fires when the strip path is already running (during ad blocking) and only blanks a specific line type that shouldn't be present in normal playback content. No new state, no new code paths.

author: aiceflower
body:
## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR fixes the DB2 schema query issue in the `getAllDatabases()` method of DB2 SqlConnection classes. The original implementation used an invalid command `list database directory` which is a DB2 CLP (Command Line Processor) command, not a valid SQL statement for JDBC execution, causing the schema list retrieval to fail.

**Changes:**
1. Replace invalid `list database directory` command with proper SQL query against `SYSCAT.SCHEMATA`
2. Add configurable schema query SQL (`wds.linkis.server.mdm.service.db2.schema.query.sql`) with default filtering system schemas (SYS%, NULLID, SQLJ)
3. Update both modules:
   - `linkis-datasource-manager/service/jdbc/src/main/java/org/apache/linkis/metadata/query/service/db2/SqlConnection.java`
   - `linkis-metadata-query/service/jdbc/src/main/java/org/apache/linkis/metadata/query/service/db2/SqlConnection.java`

Fixes #5408

## Why are the changes needed?

The `list database directory` command is a DB2 CLP command that cannot be executed via JDBC `executeQuery()`. This causes SQLException when trying to get the schema/database list from DB2 data sources.

**Brief change log:**
- Fixed `getAllDatabases()` method to use proper SQL: `SELECT SCHEMANAME FROM SYSCAT.SCHEMATA WITH UR`
- Added configurable SQL for schema query with system schema filtering
- Renamed variable from `dataBaseName` to `schemaNames` for clarity (DB2 uses schemas, not databases)

## How was this patch tested?

- Manual testing with DB2 data source connection
- Verified schema list retrieval works correctly
- Tested with both user schemas and system schemas filtering

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

- No breaking changes
- Users can configure the schema query SQL via `wds.linkis.server.mdm.service.db2.schema.query.sql` if needed

### Check List (Author)

- [x] The PR title follows format: `[fix][PES][datasource] fix DB2 schema query to use correct SQL instead of invalid command`
- [x] The PR has meaningful description
- [x] Code follows Linkis style
- [x] No new dependencies added
- [x] No breaking changes introduced
- [x] Related issue linked: Fixes #5408

This PR proposes changes to:

-  [ ] Scripts (bosses, spell scripts, creature scripts).
-  [ ] Database (SAI, creatures, etc).

When a player selects Exit Game and they are on a timed logout, if they select Exit Now, the client doesn't send an opcode for an immediate exit. As far as the server is concerned, an intentional Exit Now and an accidental connection loss is the same. This triggers a timeout period where the character stays in-world for an extra 60 seconds after Exit Now.

This change makes sure that if the character is on an intentional logout, a disconnection is recognized as intentional and the timeout period doesn't trigger, instead they only wait the 20 second countdown.

The magic number of 60 has been replaced with the value of the config DisconnectToleranceInterval. The config is about skipping the join server queue, if the player disconnected in the last X seconds. The queue is relevant if there's an overwhelming number of players trying to join. It was set to 0 (disabled) since Trinity or even before, but there's no reason for that. Since it goes hand in hand with the disconnection grace period, it was defaulted to 60 and adapted for use here too, as suggested by @pangolp.

author: chessing234
body:
## Bug

\`selective_state_update\` in \`mamba_ssm/ops/triton/selective_state_update.py\` advertises both \`D=None\` and \`dt_bias=None\` in its signature, but calling it with either one set to \`None\` raises \`TypeError\` before the kernel ever launches:

\`\`\`
TypeError: Value after * must be an iterable, not int
\`\`\`

## Root cause

The Python wrapper has two conditional-unpack expressions feeding the Triton kernel:

\`\`\`python
*(dt_bias.stride(0), dt_bias.stride(1)) if dt_bias is not None else 0,
...
*(D.stride(0), D.stride(1)) if D is not None else 0,
\`\`\`

Python parses these as

\`\`\`python
*((a, b) if cond else 0)
\`\`\`

so when the conditional is False the \`else\` branch produces the scalar \`0\`, which \`*\` then tries to unpack and fails.

Quick reproduction (just the syntax, without Triton):

\`\`\`python
def f(*args): pass
f(*(1, 2) if True else 0)    # (1, 2) — OK
f(*(1, 2) if False else 0)   # TypeError: Value after * must be an iterable, not int
\`\`\`

The two in-tree callers in \`mamba_ssm/modules/mamba_simple.py\` and \`mamba_ssm/modules/mamba2.py\` always pass non-\`None\` \`D\` and \`dt_bias\`, so the bug is latent for the standard Mamba/Mamba2 forward path. It trips as soon as anything calls \`from mamba_ssm.ops.triton.selective_state_update import selective_state_update\` and omits \`D\` or \`dt_bias\` — which is exactly the use case the public function's default-\`None\` signature advertises.

The \`tie_hdim\` line just above has the same \`dt_bias is None\` blind spot — \`dt_bias.stride(-1) == 0\` is short-circuited for the common case but becomes an \`AttributeError\` whenever \`A\` and \`dt\` also happen to have zero trailing strides (which is exactly when \`tie_hdim\` is meant to be true).

## Fix

1. Wrap the conditional expression inside each unpack with parentheses and replace \`else 0\` with \`else (0, 0)\`, so both branches yield a 2-tuple the kernel wrapper can unpack into its two stride placeholder slots (the kernel ignores those strides via the \`HAS_DT_BIAS\` / \`HAS_D\` heuristics whenever the underlying pointer is None).

2. Guard the \`tie_hdim\` check with \`dt_bias is None or dt_bias.stride(-1) == 0\` so we don't dereference a None dt_bias — a None dt_bias is trivially \"tied\" across heads because there's nothing to tie.

\`\`\`diff
-    tie_hdim = A.stride(-1) == 0 and A.stride(-2) == 0 and dt.stride(-1) == 0 and dt_bias.stride(-1) == 0
+    tie_hdim = (A.stride(-1) == 0 and A.stride(-2) == 0 and dt.stride(-1) == 0
+                and (dt_bias is None or dt_bias.stride(-1) == 0))
     with torch.cuda.device(x.device.index):
         _selective_scan_update_kernel[grid](
             ...
-            *(dt_bias.stride(0), dt_bias.stride(1)) if dt_bias is not None else 0,
+            *((dt_bias.stride(0), dt_bias.stride(1)) if dt_bias is not None else (0, 0)),
             ...
-            *(D.stride(0), D.stride(1)) if D is not None else 0,
+            *((D.stride(0), D.stride(1)) if D is not None else (0, 0)),
\`\`\`

No effect on the existing Mamba/Mamba2 forward path (both in-tree callers pass non-None \`D\` and \`dt_bias\`, so both conditionals take the \`if\` branch exactly as before). The change only affects the \`D is None\` / \`dt_bias is None\` paths, which are currently unreachable without crashing.

body:
Closes #206

## Summary

- Introduces `FOCUS_RING` constant in `src/lib/a11y.ts` as the single source of truth for keyboard focus styling
- Applies `FOCUS_RING` to every interactive element in the app (22 components) so keyboard users can always identify the focused control (WCAG 2.4.7 — Focus Visible, Level AA)
- Removes two `outline-none` anti-patterns on `<input type="search">` (RepoList, Settings) that were actively suppressing keyboard focus indicators
- Replaces one hardcoded `focus-visible:outline-blue-500` in `WorkspaceView` with the shared constant to harmonize the design

## FOCUS_RING constant

```ts
export const FOCUS_RING =
  "outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-accent focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-bg";
```

- Uses Tailwind v4 utilities backed by the project's `@theme` tokens (`--color-accent`, `--color-bg`)
- `outline-none` suppresses the browser default; the ring activates only on `:focus-visible` so mouse clicks don't show a halo
- Applied inline or through existing shared class constants (`FILTER_BUTTON_CLASS`, `ACTION_BUTTON_CLASS`, `INLINE_CONTROL_CLASS`, `controlButtonClass`) when present

## Global CSS safety net

`src/index.css` keeps a minimal `:focus-visible { outline: ... }` rule as a fallback for any interactive element that slips through in the future (third-party widgets, new components). The `box-shadow` was removed to avoid conflicting with Tailwind's ring (which itself uses `box-shadow`).

## Components updated

**Sidebar**: NavItem · Sidebar (Repos toggle, Focus mode) · RepoList (search input, buttons, checkboxes) · WorkspaceList  
**Workspace**: WorkspaceSwitcher (back + tabs) · WorkspaceView (wake button) · WorkspaceStatusBar (push/pull/github) · WorkspaceListPage  
**Cards**: MyPrCard · ReviewCard · IssueCard (links)  
**Lists**: MyPRs · ReviewQueue · Issues · ActivityFeed (filter buttons + search inputs)  
**Misc**: Overview (expand button) · Settings (NumberField, search, checkboxes, control buttons) · AuthSetup (5 interactive elements) · Toast (notification button) · ErrorBoundary (retry) · CommandPalette (search input) · WsBadge (action)

## Tests

- New `src/lib/a11y.test.ts` — 6 substring tests guarding the constant shape
- New focus-visible assertions in `NavItem.test.tsx`, `Issues.test.tsx`, `MyPRs.test.tsx`, `ActivityFeed.test.tsx` (iterates every token in `FOCUS_RING` via `toHaveClass`)
- **558 tests passing** (was 555)
- `npm run lint` — 0 warnings / 0 errors
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run build` — clean (the `a11y` module becomes a 500-byte shared chunk via Rollup dedup)

## Test plan

- [ ] Tab through every screen (Overview, Reviews, MyPRs, Issues, Activity, Workspaces, Settings) — every focused element should show a visible accent ring
- [ ] Click elements with mouse — no ring should appear (focus-visible only fires for keyboard)
- [ ] Test the RepoList search input and Settings repo search (the two inputs that previously had `outline-none`)
- [ ] Open the Command Palette (⌘K) — the search input should have the ring on focus, cmdk arrow navigation still works
- [ ] Resize to dark/light (N/A — app is dark-only) and verify ring contrast against `bg-bg`

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All interactive elements have visible focus indicators
- [x] Focus ring uses `focus-visible` (not `focus`) to avoid showing on mouse click
- [x] Focus ring contrasts sufficiently against app background (accent #c8ff00 on bg #111110 — excellent contrast)

author: evolarjun
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the pattern of checking `blob.exists()` before calling `blob.download_as_bytes()` (or `download_as_string()`) with a single direct download attempt wrapped in a `try-except google.cloud.exceptions.NotFound` block. This was applied across `index()`, `results_page()`, `return_results()`, and download endpoints (`output()`, `stderr_output()`, `nucleotide_output()`, `protein_output()`). The mock storage tests in `test_frontend.py` were updated to raise `NotFound` on failed downloads to support this new logic.

🎯 **Why:** The previous pattern incurred two separate network roundtrips to Google Cloud Storage (one to check metadata, one to download). The new pattern reduces this to a single network call for successful downloads, improving performance and efficiency.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** We reduced the number of GCS network calls for a successful file download from 2 to 1 (a 50% reduction in network overhead per download operation). (Note: Specific ms latency improvement was not benchmarked due to the mocked environment, but halving API calls directly translates to lower latency and GCS usage costs).

author: lwgray
body:
## Summary

Phase B (design artifact registration via MCP tools) has been dead code for 5 days. Design artifacts generated by Phase A never reached \`state.task_artifacts\`, so implementation tasks walking dependencies via \`_collect_task_artifacts\` found empty dicts for every design task dependency. Contract-first decomposition was silently non-functional.

**This PR is a side-quest bug fix.** It does NOT close #320. #320 PR 2 proper (\`decompose_by_contract\` + \`Task.responsibility\` + \`MARCUS_DECOMPOSER\` feature flag) is still ahead as a separate PR.

## Root Cause

Timeline:

- **2026-04-02** (#297, commit \`4daccb7\`): Two-phase design autocomplete landed. Phase A synchronous inside \`create_project_from_description\`, stored output in \`result[\"design_content\"]\`. Phase B in \`src/marcus_mcp/tools/nlp.py\` read the key after \`state.refresh_project_state()\`. Handoff worked.
- **2026-04-06** (#314, commit \`1c5c7f7\`): Phase A moved to background closure via \`asyncio.ensure_future\` to prevent Claude Code timeouts on long LLM calls. The line \`result[\"design_content\"] = design_content\` was deleted as part of the refactor. Phase B in nlp.py continued to read \`result.get(\"design_content\", {})\` — always \`{}\`. Dead code.
- **2026-04-06 → 2026-04-11**: Marcus generated design artifacts to disk on every project creation but never registered them in \`state.task_artifacts\`. Agents saw no contracts from design deps.
- **2026-04-11** (this PR): Regression discovered while planning #320 PR 2.

No existing test caught the regression. The \`TestRegisterDesignViaMcp\` unit tests mock \`design_content\` directly, bypassing the handoff.

## Fix

Consolidate Phase A and Phase B into a single module-level \`_run_design_phase\` function that runs both in lockstep inside the background task. Cannot break again without touching both phases together.

### Ordering Invariant

**Phase B registration MUST run before the kanban DONE update.** The DONE update unblocks implementation tasks from hard dependencies — if Phase B runs after, there's a sub-second window where an impl task unblocks before \`state.task_artifacts\` is populated, and the agent's dependency walk returns empty.

Ordering is pinned in \`_run_design_phase\` and tested by \`test_phase_b_registration_runs_before_kanban_done_update\`.

## Changes

### \`src/integrations/nlp_tools.py\` (+247 / -73)

- New module-level async \`_run_design_phase(state, kanban_client, safe_tasks, created_tasks, description, project_name, project_root)\` — orchestrates Phase A → Phase B → kanban DONE → scaffold in a fixed order with load-bearing ordering
- \`NaturalLanguageProjectCreator.__init__\` takes optional \`state\` param (None default for backward compat)
- Closure inside \`create_project_from_description\` replaced with direct call to \`_run_design_phase\` via \`ensure_future\`
- Fail-fast semantics: Phase A exception short-circuits the entire phase (no partial state.task_artifacts, no kanban updates, no scaffold)

### \`src/marcus_mcp/tools/nlp.py\` (-30 / +13)

- Dropped the dead Phase B block that read \`result[\"design_content\"]\`
- Both call sites now pass \`state=state\` to \`NaturalLanguageProjectCreator\`

### \`tests/unit/integrations/test_design_autocomplete.py\` (+340)

New \`TestRunDesignPhaseHandoff\` class with 4 chain-level regression tests:

1. \`test_run_design_phase_populates_state_task_artifacts\` — full chain: Phase A → Phase B → \`state.task_artifacts[design_task_id]\` populated. This is the assertion that would have caught #314's regression on day one.
2. \`test_phase_b_registration_runs_before_kanban_done_update\` — ordering invariant: Phase B \`log_artifact\` fires before \`kanban.update_task\` DONE
3. \`test_run_design_phase_handles_phase_a_failure\` — Phase A exception short-circuits, no Phase B, no kanban updates, no partial state
4. \`test_run_design_phase_noop_when_no_design_tasks\` — empty \`design_content\` is a clean no-op

### \`docs/source/systems/coordination/52-design-autocomplete.md\` (rewritten)

The old version still described the pre-#314 design (Phase A synchronous, tasks born DONE). Updated to match current code:

- Background execution model via \`ensure_future\`
- \`assigned_to=\"Marcus\"\` race mitigation (replaces \"born DONE\" invariant)
- Ordering invariant (Phase B before kanban DONE)
- **Regression History** section documenting the 5-day outage so future refactors know why the two phases were consolidated

## Test Results

- \`tests/unit/integrations/test_design_autocomplete.py\`: 15/15 passed
- \`pytest -m unit\`: 391/391 passed
- \`mypy src/integrations/nlp_tools.py src/marcus_mcp/tools/nlp.py\`: clean

## Test plan

- [x] Chain-level regression test: create_project → background Phase A → Phase B → \`state.task_artifacts\` populated
- [x] Ordering invariant test: Phase B log_artifact before kanban update_task DONE
- [x] Phase A failure: no partial state, no kanban updates, no scaffold
- [x] Empty design_content: clean no-op
- [x] Backward compat: optional \`state\` param defaults to None, legacy behavior preserved
- [x] \`pytest -m unit\` green
- [x] mypy clean on touched files
- [ ] Post-merge: run snake game with Phase B alive, verify integration_verification.py receives richer evidence

## Related

- Supersedes nothing (new PR)
- Related to #320 PR 2 (does NOT close — PR 2 proper is decomposer work still ahead)
- Regression from #314
- Built on #297's infrastructure

body:
## Summary
- rename `ec2-ubuntu.cfn.yml` to `ec2-linux.cfn.yml`
- replace the Ubuntu defaults with an Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2023 x86_64 AMI and matching documentation updates
- make `Ec2UserData` optional in both EC2 templates so CloudFormation omits `UserData` unless it is explicitly provided
- remove the Windows default bootstrap and `CreationPolicy`, and align the README and AGENTS docs with the new behavior

## Why
The branch is no longer just an arm64 image update. The current diff replaces the Ubuntu-oriented Linux template with an ECS-optimized Amazon Linux variant and simplifies both EC2 templates so bootstrapping is opt-in instead of built in.

## Impact

author: charliehess
body:
## Summary
In a consumer project testing Unity 6.6 alpha, the remaining Fast Enter Play Mode problems clustered in Extenject. Most of them came from static contexts, caches, and pools that were only safe because domain reload used to clear them between play sessions.

Unity 6.6 is moving the other way. Fast Enter Play Mode is the default for new projects, and the existing reset hooks here were still editor-gated and tied to `EditorSettings.enterPlayModeOptionsEnabled`. That left the no-domain-reload path depending on behavior that was no longer guaranteed.

This branch makes those resets explicit at `SubsystemRegistration` and adds the missing reset coverage for static memory pools plus the generic `DictionaryPool`, `HashSetPool`, and `ListPool` helpers. These are the changes we used to keep an embedded-Extenject consumer project working on Unity `6000.6.0a2` with domain reload disabled.

I am not presenting this as a complete Unity 6.6 support pass for the repository's sample project. The validation here came from the downstream consumer-project migration, and I checked in `UNITY_6_6_FAST_ENTER_PLAY_MODE_NOTES.md` to make that provenance explicit.

body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the iterative `$item->update()` calls in `ItineraryService::recalculateAfterReorder` with a single bulk `ItineraryItem::upsert()`.

🎯 **Why:** Previously, each itinerary item being recalculated triggered a separate `UPDATE` database query. For a trip with many destinations, this caused an N+1 bottleneck and degraded performance when dragging and dropping items to reorder the itinerary. Batching these into a single database transaction drastically reduces I/O.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces database `UPDATE` queries from *N* (number of itinerary items) to exactly *1* query per reordered day.

🔬 **Measurement:** Execute `php artisan test --filter SmartItineraryTest` to verify that calculations remain correct, and observe the database query logs during a `PUT /api/itineraries/{id}/reorder` API request to confirm the reduced query count.

author: thomaspoisson31
body:
Resolves a bug where creating items (characters, tables, journal entries) on one device and loading the session on a second device would result in lost data.

The issue stemmed from two root causes:
1. `CharactersManager` explicitly didn't include `globalData.characters` in the `dynamicData` payload generated for standard (non-standalone) campaigns inside `AuthManager.collectCurrentContextData`. Thus, characters were effectively ignored during standard saves.
2. A concurrency/race condition where `applyContextData` would rapidly load various sub-managers (like Counters, Calendars, Characters). Many of those managers execute `this.save()` internally upon initialization/loading, which inadvertently schedules an automatic cloud sync *using stale or incomplete local data*. This triggered an immediate, background upload that quietly wiped out the rest of the cloud payload just as the user had requested to download it. 

To fix this:
* `AuthManager` now guards `scheduleAutoSync` and `syncUserData` explicitly with `isLoadingFromCloud` and a newly introduced `window.isApplyingCloudData` flag.
* `AuthManager` formally extracts and attaches `globalData.characters` in the final return payload for campaigns.
* `AuthManager.applyContextData` manually commits the loaded `characters` explicitly to `localStorage` ensuring it's available after immediate page refreshes.

---

author: mrrayg
body:
## Summary

- **Replace blind `.slice()` KB context** with `semanticSearch()` from `embeddingEngine.ts` in three functions — each hypothesis/entry now gets the most semantically relevant KB entries instead of arbitrary first-N entries
- **`autoResolveHypotheses()`**: moved kbContext inside the hypothesis loop; uses `semanticSearch("${hyp.claim} ${hyp.prediction}", { maxResults: 15 })` per hypothesis
- **`autoTestHypotheses()`**: same pattern with `maxResults: 30` for the evaluation pipeline
- **`checkContradictions()` in `reasoningEngine.ts`**: contradiction candidates are now the 30 most semantically similar entries to the new entry
- All three locations fall back gracefully to the original blind-slice approach if semantic search fails or returns empty
- Added logging for monitoring semantic search relevance scores

## Why This Matters

The existing embedding engine (`embeddingEngine.ts`) with `semanticSearch()` was already built and working, but hypothesis evaluation was ignoring it entirely. Every hypothesis got identical context — the first 15 active KB entries regardless of topic. This meant a hypothesis about "AI chip manufacturing" would get the same KB entries as one about "social media sentiment," making the LLM evaluate with irrelevant context.

## Rate Limit Notes

- Each hypothesis triggers one embedding API call for the query text
- KB entry embeddings are cached in `knowledge_embeddings.json` — only query embeddings are computed per-hypothesis
- The existing 5s delay between hypothesis resolution iterations and the embedding engine's built-in 1000ms rate limit provide natural spacing
- With 50 hypotheses max, this adds ~50 embedding calls per cycle — well within typical API limits

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify TypeScript compiles cleanly (`npm run check` — no new errors in modified files)
- [ ] Run a daily cycle and check logs for `[DailyCycle] Semantic KB context for` messages showing per-hypothesis relevance scores
- [ ] Verify fallback works: temporarily break embedding API key and confirm hypotheses still resolve with fallback context
- [ ] Check that contradiction detection logs show `[Reasoning] Semantic contradiction candidates` with relevance scores

author: copilot
body:
`root_get_handler` allocates a 6 KiB buffer on the `httpd` task stack (default ~4 KiB), causing a Stack Protection Fault on every web UI request.

```
Guru Meditation Error: Core 0 panic'ed (Stack protection fault)
Detected in task "httpd" at 0x400257f8
--- root_get_handler at web_server.c:219
```

### Changes

- **Heap-allocate the HTML render buffer** — `char buf[6144]` → `malloc`/`free`, keeping the 6 KiB buffer off the task stack
- **Increase httpd task stack to 8 KiB** — `config.stack_size = 8192` for margin against future handler growth
- **Clamp `snprintf` return value** — prevent passing an oversize length to `httpd_resp_send` if output is ever truncated

### Motivation
- Patch an authentication bypass where `/embed/dify/token` could mint signed proxy tokens based only on client-supplied `Origin`/`Referer` headers, allowing non-browser clients to obtain valid tokens by header spoofing.

### Description
- Require possession of the configured static proxy secret header (`X-Embed-Proxy-Token`) in `handleDifyProxyToken` before issuing signed tokens.

author: tuwebti
body:
Hi @ahyatt,

I've been thinking about your comment in #299. It seems to me there are two desirable properties here:

1. Tests should run in a clean environment, so they do not silently interact with existing user state.
2. Tests should fail if they try to connect to a database without one being explicitly provided.

This PR is an attempt at addressing **(1)** by making sure tests run with potentially dangerous variables `let`-bound to safe values.

Property **(2)** would also be useful, because it would give us a clean way to ensure some functionality does not depend on mutable database state, but it is a bit trickier to implement in practice.

## 1. Run tests in a clean environment

### Motivation

We want `ekg` tests to avoid interfering with any pre-existing user state. To do that, they should all run in a clean environment where potentially dangerous global variables are `let`-bound to safe values.

For tests that require a database, we explicitly set one up with `ekg-deftest-with-db`.

### Changes in this PR

In `ekg-test-utils`:

* `ekg-deftest` now only `let`-binds dangerous variables, it doesn't set up a database connection anymore.
* `ekg-deftest-with-db` was added to also set up a database connection. That is, it does what ekg-deftest used to do.

I then ran:

```sh
find . -type f -name '*test.el' \
  -exec sed -i 's/ekg-deftest/ekg-deftest-with-db/g' {} +
```

```sh
find . -type f -name '*test.el' \
  -exec sed -i 's/ert-deftest/ekg-deftest/g' {} +
```

and made sure that all `*test.el` files require `ekg-test-utils`.

## Why (2) is tricky

As things currently stand, even if a test uses `ekg-deftest` rather than `ekg-deftest-with-db`, `ekg-connect` still works. That is because `ekg-connect`, `triples-connect`, and `sqlite-open` are all a little too helpful.

To stop `ekg-connect` from silently connecting to an existing database, you need to `let`-bind:

* `ekg-db`
* `ekg-db-file`
* `triples-default-database-filename`

Even then, `sqlite-open` will still silently open an in-memory database.

Given that `ekg-deftest` currently `let`-binds `ekg-db-file` to a temporary test database, this is not too serious, since we are at least no longer silently testing against an existing user database. Still, it does bother me a bit that `ekg-connect` can keep working even when a database was not explicitly provided for the test.

## Summary
`save_ingr_chests` blocked the main thread for 170ms serializing ~12000 objects.

**Before:** Main thread serializes all objects → writes files → 170ms lag spike.

**After:** Main thread copies object pointers (microseconds) → detaches background thread → thread serializes + writes → 0ms on main thread.

Objects stay alive in the chest between saves, so raw pointers are safe for the detached thread.

body:
🚨 **Severity**: MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability**: The script `run_once_before_install-packages-darwin.sh.tmpl` used an unsafe command substitution: `if test ! $(which brew); then`. If `which brew` is not found, the output is empty, leading to `test !`, which is a syntax error in Bash (`bash: test: !: unary operator expected`) and causes unpredictable execution flow. Furthermore, it relied on an external command (`which`) instead of a shell built-in.
🎯 **Impact**: The script could fail or bypass the Homebrew installation step, resulting in unpredictable environment setup. It also exhibited a pattern prone to word-splitting and command injection if path resolutions were tampered with.
🔧 **Fix**: Replaced the unsafe check with the POSIX-compliant `command -v` shell built-in: `if ! command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then`.
✅ **Verification**: Run `bash -n` on the modified script to ensure correct syntax, and ran the full suite of checks to ensure no regressions. A new Sentinel journal entry was also added.

author: aakashlpin
body:
## Summary
The Multica agent picker in the menu bar panel was permanently stuck on "No Multica agents available" even though `multica agent list --output json` returns two valid agents and `MulticaAgentRegistry.refreshAvailableAgents()` successfully populates.

Root cause: the panel read the agent list via Mirror reflection on `companionManager`. That was written back in AAK-7 as a forward-compatible stub, when `multicaAgentRegistry` did not yet exist on `CompanionManager`. Now that AAK-9 has landed the real property, the reflection approach has two problems:

1. **SwiftUI never re-renders when `availableAgents` updates.** `@Published private(set) var multicaAgentRegistry` on `CompanionManager` only fires when the registry reference itself is reassigned — not when a nested `@Published availableAgents` array on the registry changes. Mirror reads are one-shot snapshots at render time, so the view captures whatever was in `availableAgents` at panel-open and never re-renders.
2. **The dead fallback branch** (an untyped Mirror walk through `availableAgents` children) is no longer reachable and just adds noise.

## Fix
- Add `@ObservedObject var multicaAgentRegistry: MulticaAgentRegistry` directly on `CompanionPanelView`.
- Wire it from `MenuBarPanelManager.createPanel()` by passing `companionManager.multicaAgentRegistry`.
- Replace `multicaAvailableAgentNames`'s Mirror walk with a one-liner: `multicaAgentRegistry.availableAgents.map(\.name)`.
- Add `.task { await multicaAgentRegistry.refreshAvailableAgents() }` on panel appearance, so the user gets fresh data every time the menu bar panel opens (and sees new agents they added mid-session without having to restart Clicky).

## Test plan
- [x] `./scripts/build-launcher.sh` archives clean
- [ ] Open the menu bar panel → flip "Delegation target" to "Multica" → the "Default agent" picker now shows "Planning agent" and "SSE Agent" instead of "No Multica agents available"

body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce time-based candle aggregation for trading, retraining, and dashboard visuals, switch duration logic from ticks to minutes with adaptive retraining, and harden the dashboard API and trading logic with new filters, preloading, and tests.

New Features:
- Support time-based candles throughout the bot, pipeline, indicators, and dashboard, including server endpoints that aggregate ticks into OHLC candles by time.
- Add adaptive retraining logic that triggers model updates based on win rate, confidence, new data volume, and time-based backstops instead of fixed intervals.
- Expose richer dashboard visualizations such as linear-time price/contract charts, RSI/MACD history from a new indicator-series API, and ROC-AUC model comparison.
- Enable duration prediction in minutes using updated candidate durations and integrate ensemble TFT/classical models with confidence gating.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix contract timeout and polling delays to correctly treat durations as minutes instead of ticks, preventing premature or delayed result checks.
- Correct handling of existing candle/tick history on reconnect and during dataset building to avoid duplicated or misaligned data and degenerate candles.
- Ensure dashboard JSON responses are always valid by sanitizing NaN/Inf and tighten dashboard authentication to reject unauthenticated non-local control requests.
- Resolve issues where AI predictions could be used with too-low confidence or degenerate indicator inputs, improving signal gating and avoiding crashes.

Enhancements:
- Refine entry cadence to operate on closed time-based candles with optional candle-pattern filters, and update indicator thresholds (RSI/ADX) and scoring weights for more selective entries.
- Preload historical candles from CSV/API on bot startup to eliminate long warmup periods and seed ADX history for more stable initial behavior.
- Improve dataset building and training to work natively on time-based candles, adjust feature windows and volatility-based duration heuristics, and persist richer model-metrics including cross-model ROC-AUC.
- Strengthen strategy edge handling with better behavior on flat, noisy, or NaN-containing price series, and integrate candle pattern alerts as a soft conflict filter in the signal pipeline.

Build:
- Add VS Code workspace settings and update config defaults for time-based candles, candidate durations, AI weights, and adaptive retraining thresholds.

Documentation:
- Update README to document time-based candles, revised duration candidates, scoring and target lookforward parameters, and champion-challenger promotion criteria.

Tests:
- Add integration and unit tests for pipeline thresholds, server endpoints, trading flow, strategy edge cases, and configuration invariants to guard recommended settings and API behavior.
- Extend existing tests to assert recommended config for candle timeframe, target lookforward, signal thresholds, and training metrics path handling.

Chores:
- Adjust dashboard backend shebang and add lightweight PID/log artifacts for local development.

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip orchestrates AI agents for zero-human companies
> - Local development depends on execution workspaces and helper scripts that can launch services without disturbing the main working tree
> - When dev runner processes inherit the wrong worktree environment, they can bind themselves to the active checkout instead of the intended isolated workspace
> - That makes branch-splitting and multi-worktree workflows fragile, especially when a long-running dev server is already using the main checkout
> - This pull request isolates dev runner worktree environment handling in one helper and adds coverage around the workspace path/env resolution rules
> - The benefit is safer local execution from alternate worktrees without accidentally contaminating the primary dev workspace

## What Changed

- Added a dedicated server helper for deriving isolated dev-runner worktree environment values

author: the-r4v3n
body:
## Problem

Triggering two manual workflow runs in quick succession caused a race condition. Both runs:
1. Completed ORACLE/AXIOM analysis and wrote session #146 journals
2. Both modified `memory/sessions.json` and `docs/index.html`
3. The second run's `git pull --rebase --autostash` popped the stash on top of the first run's changes, creating unresolved merge conflicts

Result: conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) were committed directly into `sessions.json` (42 markers) and `docs/index.html` (8 markers), breaking the GitHub Pages site and all subsequent `rebuild-site` calls.

## Fix

- Restored `memory/sessions.json` from the clean 13:07 UTC commit (valid JSON, 146 sessions)
- Rebuilt `docs/index.html` from scratch via `npm run rebuild-site`
- Net result: 289 lines of conflict noise removed, site restored

## Root cause (separate issue)

The concurrent workflow runs are caused by triggering multiple manual dispatches. The `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: false` setting queues rather than cancels, so both runs execute sequentially on the same session number. Consider adding conflict-resistant HTML generation (atomic temp file + rename) as a follow-up.

author: hedjav
body:
## Problème vu en prod

Client a payé via FedaPay, a vu la confirmation, **mais** :
- \`/dashboard/mes-ebooks\` affiche \"Vous n'avez pas encore acheté d'ebook\"
- Quand il tente de racheter, \`/api/purchases/create\` répond \"Ebook déjà acheté\"
- Aucun bouton de téléchargement visible

## Diagnostic

3 incohérences croisées :

| Route | Client utilisé | Filtre | Résultat |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`GET /api/purchases/check\` | user session | \`user_id = uid()\` uniquement | \`purchased: false\` |
| \`POST /api/purchases/create\` | service-role | \`user_id = uid()\` uniquement (avant ce PR) | \`409 Ebook déjà acheté\` |
| \`/dashboard/mes-ebooks\` | user session | \`user_id OR email\` + join \`ebook\` filtré par RLS | 0 ebook |

Cause racine : la RLS sur \`purchases\` et/ou la RLS \`is_published=true\` sur \`ebooks\` masquait des lignes au user session, ET le \`.filter(p => p.ebook !== null)\` dans \`queries.ts\` droppait les achats dont l'ebook avait été dépublié. Du coup :
- L'achat existe réellement en DB (service-role le voit)
- Le user authentifié ne le voit pas (RLS ou join null)
- Le check dit \"non acheté\", le create dit \"déjà acheté\", mes-ebooks dit \"vide\"

## Fix

### 1. Queries homogènes en service-role (\`lib/purchases/queries.ts\`)

Toutes les fonctions de lecture purchases utilisent maintenant le client \`service-role\`. On vérifie la session user côté serveur AVANT, donc zéro risque sécurité : on ne lit que les purchases du user authentifié via \`user_id OR email\`.

Nouvelle fonction \`getCurrentUserPendingPurchases()\` qui retourne les achats \`pending\`/\`failed\` pour transparence (quand un webhook FedaPay a foiré et que le client s'inquiète).

Nouveau type \`PaidPurchaseView\` où \`ebook\` peut être \`null\` — on ne drop plus les achats dont l'ebook a disparu.

### 2. Check et Create cohérents

- \`GET /api/purchases/check\` : service-role + match \`user_id OR email\` (même logique que \`/create\`)
- \`POST /api/purchases/create\` : match \`user_id OR email\`, réponse 409 enrichie avec \`{error, message, action: {label, href}, purchase_id}\`

Plus jamais de divergence entre les deux routes.

### 3. UI dashboard avec 3 sections

\`/dashboard/mes-ebooks\` affiche maintenant :

1. **Bandeau rouge** si \`?download_error=CODE\` (déjà fait dans PR #59)
2. **Section orange** \"Commandes en attente de validation\" — pending/failed purchases avec la référence FedaPay à citer au support
3. **Section bleue** \"Achats en attente de fichier\" — purchases paid dont l'ebook est null (supprimé/dépublié), avec email de contact
4. **Grille principale** — ebooks téléchargeables normaux

Plus jamais de \"vous n'avez pas encore acheté d'ebook\" quand une purchase existe réellement.

### 4. Outils admin pour réparer manuellement

Pour débloquer ce client immédiatement :

**\`GET /api/admin/purchases/diagnose?email=client@xxx\`**
Retourne toutes les purchases du client + diagnostic par row + diagnostic global :
- \`✓ OK\` si tout est en ordre
- \`⚠ Status = pending\` si webhook FedaPay raté
- \`⚠ user_id = null\` si purchase pré-auth non liée
- \`⚠ Ebook dépublié\`
- \`⚠ Pas de file_path\`
- \`✗ Ebook supprimé\`

On peut aussi filtrer par \`purchase_id\` ou \`user_id\`.

**\`POST /api/admin/purchases/repair\`** — 3 actions pour débloquer

\`\`\`json
{ \"purchase_id\": \"uuid\", \"action\": \"mark_paid\" }
\`\`\`
Force le status à \`paid\` (quand le webhook FedaPay a raté mais le paiement est confirmé FedaPay Dashboard)

\`\`\`json
{ \"purchase_id\": \"uuid\", \"action\": \"link_user\", \"target_email\": \"client@xxx\" }
\`\`\`
Lie la purchase à un compte Supabase existant (quand la purchase a \`user_id=null\`)

\`\`\`json
{ \"purchase_id\": \"uuid\", \"action\": \"resend_email\" }
\`\`\`
Renvoie l'email de confirmation avec le lien direct de téléchargement

## Procédure pour le client bloqué

Une fois cette PR mergée et déployée :

1. \`GET /api/admin/purchases/diagnose?email={email_du_client}\` dans le navigateur admin
2. Identifier la purchase qui coince (colonne \`diagnostic\`)
3. Selon le diagnostic :
   - \`status=pending\` → vérifier FedaPay Dashboard si le paiement est réellement confirmé, puis \`POST /repair action=mark_paid\`
   - \`user_id=null\` → \`POST /repair action=link_user\` avec l'email du client
   - \`Ebook dépublié\` → republier l'ebook (\`is_published=true\`) dans /admin/ebooks
   - \`Pas de file_path\` → uploader le PDF dans /admin/ebooks/[id]
4. Demander au client de rafraîchir \`/dashboard/mes-ebooks\` → il doit maintenant voir son achat
5. (Optionnel) \`POST /repair action=resend_email\` pour renvoyer un email de confirmation avec le lien de download

## Ce qui n'est PAS dans cette PR

- ❌ Nouvelle migration SQL (les policies RLS existantes sont conservées, on les bypass côté serveur au lieu de les toucher)
- ❌ Modification du webhook FedaPay (le bug est dans la lecture pas l'écriture)
- ❌ Modification de l'upload admin

## Test plan

- [ ] TypeScript clean ✅
- [ ] Un user avec purchase paid + ebook publié + file_path OK voit l'ebook dans son dashboard
- [ ] Un user avec purchase paid + ebook dépublié voit la section bleue \"Achats en attente de fichier\"
- [ ] Un user avec purchase pending voit la section orange \"Commandes en attente de validation\"
- [ ] \`GET /api/purchases/check\` et \`POST /api/purchases/create\` retournent toujours la même réponse (cohérence)
- [ ] Le 409 \"déjà acheté\" contient un champ \`action\` avec un lien vers \`/dashboard/mes-ebooks\`
- [ ] \`GET /api/admin/purchases/diagnose?email=XXX\` retourne un rapport complet
- [ ] \`POST /api/admin/purchases/repair\` avec les 3 actions fonctionne
