author: tekgnosis-net
body:
## Summary

First sub-PR of Phase 6 — the biggest phase in the v1.0.0 overhaul. Scoped tightly to **backend API routes only**: settings persistence with Pydantic validation, SMTP password encryption at rest, and the three housekeeping operations (db-info / vacuum / purge). No frontend changes, no scheduler, no actual email sending — those land in 6b and 6c.

## Why split Phase 6 into sub-PRs?

The original plan's Phase 6 would have added ~4000 LOC across 7 subsystems (settings, crypto, render, mailer, scheduler, frontend, collector integration). That's too big for meaningful review. Splitting into three sub-PRs keeps each review bounded to ~1500 LOC and each sub-PR is independently mergeable — landing 6a on main leaves the app in a working state where the Phase 4 placeholder Settings view just isn't yet consuming the new routes.

- **6a (this PR)** — settings + housekeeping routes, ~1600 LOC
- **6b (next)** — email rendering + mailer + scheduler subprocess
- **6c (last)** — frontend Settings/Report views + collector integration + Dockerfile

## What's new (6.1 — settings infrastructure)

### `src/reporting/settings.py` (261 LOC)
Pydantic models for every section of `settings.json` with per-field range validation (from the Phase-6 hardcoded-to-configurable audit in the plan). Exports:
- `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` — hardcoded defaults matching pre-overhaul container behavior (interval=4, retention=3d, etc.)
- `Settings` root Pydantic model with 8 subsections
- `load_settings(path)` — deep-merges file over defaults, validates, falls back to defaults on any error
- `save_settings(path, data)` — atomic tempfile + `os.replace` write, mode 0600

### `src/reporting/crypto.py` (147 LOC)
Fernet wrapper for SMTP password at rest. Key lifecycle:
1. `GPU_MONITOR_SECRET` env var if set (for users who manage secrets externally)
2. `/app/history/.secret` if it exists
3. Generate fresh key, write with mode 0600, return

Raises `CryptoError` (not cryptography's raw `InvalidToken`) so callers have a single exception type.

### `src/server.py` — 3 new routes
- **GET `/api/settings`** — returns merged settings with `smtp.password_enc` replaced by a boolean `smtp.password_set`. **Password ciphertext never leaves the server.**
- **PUT `/api/settings`** — deep-merge partial update, Pydantic validation, Fernet-encrypts SMTP password transition, atomic write
- **POST `/api/settings/smtp/test`** — **stubbed as 501** until 6b lands the mailer. Route is registered now so the frontend can start wiring up the Test button.

### SMTP password transition sentinel

Four-way handling in PUT:

| Field state | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Absent | Preserve existing `password_enc` |
| `null` | Preserve (explicit no-change) |
| `""` | Clear ciphertext |
| `"secret"` | Encrypt with Fernet, store as `password_enc` |

This avoids the "edit one SMTP field without re-typing the password" footgun.

## What's new (6.2 — housekeeping)

- **GET `/api/housekeeping/db-info`** — returns size, row count, oldest/newest epoch, per-GPU breakdown
- **POST `/api/housekeeping/vacuum`** — runs SQLite VACUUM with `isolation_level = None` (required — VACUUM can't run in a transaction), reports `size_before/size_after/freed_bytes`
- **POST `/api/housekeeping/purge`** — body `{"days": N}` with `1 ≤ N ≤ 365`, DELETE rows older than N days, returns `rows_deleted`

New `_open_db_readwrite()` helper with 30s timeout (vs 5s for readonly) because VACUUM holds the write lock for the duration.

## Defense-in-depth

- **Same-origin header check** on all mutating routes (PUT `/api/settings`, POST vacuum/purge/smtp-test). Returns 403 on cross-origin. LAN-only defense; documented in the handler comment.
- **`settings.json` written with mode 0600** via atomic tempfile + `os.replace`.
- **Fernet key file mode 0600** on first-run generation, written via tempfile + rename so a partial write never leaves a readable zero-byte file.
- **Password ciphertext never in GET responses** — redaction happens in a helper before serialization.
- **Pydantic validates structural shape + numeric bounds**; SQL routes trust the model, not raw user input.

## Test coverage (30 new tests, 47 total)

`tests/test_crypto.py` (7 tests):
- Env var overrides file lookup
- First-run creates key with mode 0600
- Existing key file is read, not regenerated
- Encrypt/decrypt round-trip
- Empty plaintext sentinel round-trips as empty
- Wrong-key decrypt raises CryptoError (not raw InvalidToken)
- Invalid key material raises CryptoError

`tests/test_settings_api.py` (12 tests):
- First-run GET returns defaults + `password_set: false`
- PUT partial merge preserves other sections
- PUT invalid interval returns 400 with field detail
- PUT invalid JSON returns 400
- PUT body not object returns 400
- SMTP password transition: new/absent/null/empty all do the right thing
- PUT smtp.password wrong type returns 400
- Cross-origin PUT returns 403
- SMTP test endpoint returns 501 stub

`tests/test_housekeeping.py` (11 tests):
- db-info returns row count + per-GPU on seeded fixture
- Purge deletes old rows
- Purge with large days deletes nothing
- Purge is idempotent (2× call → second is zero)
- Purge rejects non-integer days (string/float/bool/None/list)
- Purge rejects out-of-range days (0/-1/366/1000)
- Purge rejects missing body
- Vacuum after purge reclaims bytes
- Vacuum on fresh DB is safe (freed ≈ 0)
- Vacuum + purge reject cross-origin

All 47 tests pass in a `python:3.11-slim` throwaway container with `pip install aiohttp pytest pytest-asyncio pydantic cryptography`.

## New dependencies

Added to the test install matrix (Dockerfile update lands in 6c alongside matplotlib / jinja / premailer):
- `pydantic` (v2) — settings validation
- `cryptography` — Fernet for SMTP password at rest

## Out of scope for this PR (6b / 6c)

- Email rendering (Jinja + matplotlib + premailer) — 6b
- `aiosmtplib` mailer — 6b
- Standalone `scheduler.py` subprocess — 6b
- `src/monitor_gpu.sh` supervisor for the scheduler — 6b
- `src/web/views/settings.js` Lit form — 6c
- `src/web/views/report.js` iframe preview — 6c
- Collector integration for live-reload of `logging.*` / `housekeeping.*` — 6c
- Dockerfile pip install matrix update — 6c
- CHANGELOG entry — added in 6c to describe the whole Phase 6 arc

## Test plan

- [x] Full pytest suite passes (47/47)
- [x] Crypto unit tests pass on stdlib-only imports
- [x] Cross-origin defense works on all mutating routes
- [ ] Manual: `docker build` with pydantic + cryptography, curl GET /api/settings, verify `smtp.password_set` is `false` and no `password_enc` leaks
- [ ] Manual: curl PUT /api/settings with partial body, verify atomic write + file mode 0600
- [ ] Manual: seed a DB, curl POST /api/housekeeping/purge, confirm rows_deleted count

## Reviewer note

Pre-enumerated risk areas Copilot is most likely to raise:

1. **`_origin_is_same` with absent Origin header** — I return `True` because direct curl / older browsers don't set Origin. Could be argued as a bypass; the alternative (requiring Origin) breaks legitimate CLI usage. LAN-only defense, documented as such.

2. **Pydantic model + deep-merge interaction** — the merge happens on a raw dict, then Pydantic validates the result. A clever PUT body could theoretically stash data in a field Pydantic ignores. Mitigation: the validated `model_dump(by_alias=True)` is what gets written to disk, so extra keys are stripped.

3. **Password clear sentinel semantics** — `""` clears, `null` preserves, absent preserves. This four-way table is tested exhaustively but worth double-checking the comment block for clarity.

4. **VACUUM `isolation_level = None`** — required for VACUUM but modifies connection state mid-request. The connection is closed in the `finally` so it can't leak, but it's worth flagging as a non-obvious necessary hack.

author: miohtama
body:
## Why

Hyper AI live startup was producing noisy compatibility warnings and stale vault logs that were hard to interpret. We needed to preserve the existing warning-first behaviour while making it clearer whether the issue was old source data, filtering, or daily resampling, and also restore compatibility with older state files and the newer strategy parameter naming used by `hyper-ai.py`.

## Lessons learnt

The vault history path already had the right home for structured diagnostics in `tradeexecutor.ethereum.vault.checks`, so extending that path kept logs and charts aligned instead of creating a second diagnostics track. Also, using a lightweight `HEAD` request kept the remote metadata check local to `trade-executor` and avoided pushing new API surface into the `trading-strategy` submodule.

## Summary

- added vault history startup diagnostics covering local cache age, remote object metadata, parquet freshness before filtering, freshness after filtering, and freshness after daily resampling
- logged the new vault freshness summary before the stale-vault warning, clarified that `1d` resampling floors candle timestamps to `00:00 UTC`, and collapsed per-vault stale entries into a single warning to avoid log spam
- propagated vault history diagnostics through all relevant `TradingStrategyUniverse` construction paths, including `clone()`, so charts and copied universes keep the same diagnostics context
- derived the cached vault-history parquet path directly instead of refetching it through the client transport fetch path
- accepted both `slippage_tolerance` and `slippage_tolerance_pct` during live startup parameter resolution
- kept `TradingPairIdentifier.exchange_address` optional for older state JSON compatibility, documented the intended runtime behaviour, and improved its fallback string representation
- added focused tests for cache-hit, stale-source, remote-HEAD-failure, resample-boundary, and diagnostics-propagation cases

author: zachtjohnson01
body:
Fixes the "Lotte from Gadgetville" problem reported in the last turn. OMDB returns IMDb's primary-language title ("Leiutajateküla Lotte") for foreign-origin films, and there's no way via the OMDB API to get the English release title. You linked Lotte to its Estonian original, but the header now shows "Leiutajateküla Lotte" and the RT link searches for the Estonian name (which RT doesn't know by that name, even though they do have the movie at `rottentomatoes.com/m/lotte_from_gadgetville`).

## Answer to "Does OMDB have this info?"

No. OMDB is a thin wrapper around IMDb's primary metadata and does not return IMDb's "also known as" / regional title data. **TMDB does** (via `/movie/{id}/alternative_titles`), but adding TMDB as a second API provider for one edge case is overkill. Simpler to just let the user override the display.

## New field: `displayTitle: string | null`

A nullable override on the `Movie` type. When set, it's used everywhere a human-readable title is shown in the UI. `title` stays as the OMDB canonical so `imdbId` linking, refresh, and the close-match filter in bulk-link all keep working against IMDb's primary record.

## Where the display override applies

All via a new `getDisplayTitle(movie)` helper in `format.ts` that returns `displayTitle?.trim() || title`:

- **Detail screen header** — you now see "Lotte from Gadgetville" instead of "Leiutajateküla Lotte"
- **WatchedList / Wishlist row titles**
- **MoviePoster placeholder** (first letter fallback for unlinked movies)
- **Delete confirm dialog** — `Delete "Lotte from Gadgetville"? This can't be undone.`
- **BulkLinkSheet** — progress view, skipped list, failed list

Plus sorting and search:

- **Undated alphabetical sort** (Watched tab, sortWatched) uses `getDisplayTitle`
- **Wishlist alphabetical sort** uses `getDisplayTitle`
- **Search boxes on both tabs** match against BOTH the canonical title AND the display override, so searching "Lotte" finds a movie stored as "Leiutajateküla Lotte" with a `displayTitle` override

## Where the canonical title stays

Preserved so the OMDB plumbing keeps working:

- `linkByTitle` / `searchMovies` (OMDB queries use the canonical title)
- `updateMovie` key lookup (the stored title is still the row identifier)
- `BulkLinkSheet`'s inner `patch.title` identity tracking
- The `Title` field in the Edit form (still maps to canonical `title`)

## URL helpers get smarter

`rottenTomatoesUrl`, `commonSenseUrl`, and the imdbUrl search-fallback now use `displayTitle ?? title` for the query string:

```ts
function searchTitle(movie: Pick<Movie, 'title' | 'displayTitle'>): string {
  const override = movie.displayTitle?.trim();
  return override || movie.title;
}
```

So tapping the RT chip on Lotte-with-override lands on `rottentomatoes.com/search?search=Lotte+from+Gadgetville` instead of the Estonian original that RT doesn't know by that name.

The IMDb chip still deep-links via `imdbId` directly when linked — unchanged.

## New: "Display title (optional)" field in the Edit form

Appears below the main Title field with this help text:

> Overrides how the movie is shown in the app. Useful when OMDB has an original-language title (like "Leiutajateküla Lotte") but you watched the English release. Leave blank to use the title above.

Leaving it blank persists as `null` via the existing `updateStr` helper, so the movie falls back to the canonical `title` for display.

## Your workflow for Lotte

1. Merge this PR → force-quit PWA → reopen
2. Open the Lotte movie → **Edit**
3. Leave the Title field as "Leiutajateküla Lotte" (that's what OMDB/IMDb know it as, keeps the imdbId linkage valid)
4. Scroll to the new **Display title** field → type "Lotte from Gadgetville"
5. **Save**
6. Back on Detail, you should see "Lotte from Gadgetville" as the header and the year still shows, Linked badge still shows, but everything the user-facing reads "Lotte from Gadgetville"
7. Tap the RT chip → lands on rottentomatoes.com/search?search=Lotte+from+Gadgetville → finds it

## Seed migration

All 40 existing movies got `displayTitle: null` added. You can apply overrides selectively — I'd suggest Lotte for sure, Arco if it has a similar original-language / English split, and any other Ghibli-like foreign-origin films where you prefer the English release name.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [ ] Set displayTitle on Lotte → header, list rows, RT chip all reflect the override
- [ ] Search "Lotte" in the Watched search box → finds the movie (match against displayTitle)
- [ ] Search "Leiut" in the Watched search box → still finds the movie (match against canonical title)
- [ ] Wishlist alphabetical sort puts the movie under its display title's first letter
- [ ] Refresh from OMDB still fetches by imdbId — title doesn't revert to OMDB canonical (displayTitle override is preserved)
- [ ] Delete confirm shows the display title

## Design note for future

If this edge case grows beyond a handful of movies, the next step would be integrating TMDB as a source of record for `/movie/{id}/alternative_titles` and auto-populating `displayTitle` based on the user's preferred locale. For a family tracker with maybe 2-3 foreign-origin films, manual override is the right level of complexity.

author: davidkonigsberg
body:
## Description

Fixes the `test-remote-vs-local-generation-parity` CI workflow, which has been consistently failing for `go-sdk` since ~April 9 (when go-sdk `1.33.6` was published).

## Root Cause

`DynamicSnippetsGeneratorContext.buildEffectiveConfig()` unconditionally overrode the output mode's `version` with `publishInfo.version` from the dynamic IR. This version reflects the **generator's own version** (e.g., `1.34.3`), not the **SDK version** being generated (e.g., `7.7.7` from the `--version` flag).

This caused `resolveRootImportPath` to compute wrong Go major version suffixes. For example, wire test imports would reference `github.com/fern-api/empty/v1/client` (from generator version `1.x`) instead of `github.com/fern-api/empty/v7/client` (from SDK version `7.x`), breaking `go mod tidy`.

The `WireTestGenerator` creates a `DynamicSnippetsGenerator` internally, so every wire test file was affected.

## Changes Made

- Preserve the original config's output mode version (set by `--version` flag during generation) when available, falling back to `publishInfo.version` only when the original config doesn't have one
- Added unreleased changelog entry

## Testing

- Reproduced locally by generating with `--version 7.7.7` and generator version `99.99.99` — confirmed `go mod tidy` fails with `github.com/fern-api/empty/v99` imports before the fix
- Verified the fix resolves the failure — generation completes successfully after the change

## Key Review Points

- The `originalVersion ?? publishInfo.version` fallback: verify this is correct for **all** callers of `DynamicSnippetsGeneratorContext` (wire tests, README snippets, FDR/docs snippets), not just the wire test path
- When the original config has a `github` or `publish` output mode, the original version now takes precedence — confirm this doesn't break the FDR/docs snippet use case described in the `buildEffectiveConfig` docstring

author: penserai
body:
## Summary

Phase 4a of the [Alertmanager feature parity plan](https://github.com/penserai/acteon/blob/main/docs/design-alertmanager-parity.md): closes gap #4 by shipping a first-class `acteon-opsgenie` provider crate and wiring it into the server's TOML provider config.

OpsGenie is the single highest-demand missing receiver for teams migrating off Alertmanager — Atlassian's incident-management platform is the default on-call tool for most customers, and without it Acteon cannot be a drop-in replacement.

## What changed

**New crate `acteon-opsgenie`** — implements the [OpsGenie Alert API v2](https://docs.opsgenie.com/docs/alert-api) with:

- **Regions**: US (`api.opsgenie.com`) and EU (`api.eu.opsgenie.com`) selectable via TOML. Accounts are pinned to one region at provisioning time so picking the wrong one surfaces as a 401.
- **Lifecycle**: a single provider handles the full `create → acknowledge → close` sequence by branching on the payload's `event_action` field. Acknowledge and close always use `identifierType=alias` so operators can use the same alias they used at create time without reading back alert IDs.
- **Defaults**: optional `opsgenie_default_team`, `opsgenie_default_priority`, and `opsgenie_default_source` fields in the TOML config materialize into the alert body when the payload omits them, keeping rule payloads short.
- **Client-side guards**: `message` is truncated to the API's 130-char limit; alias is percent-encoded in the lifecycle path segment; `ENC[...]` API keys are transparently decrypted at startup.
- **Error mapping**: 401/403 → non-retryable `Configuration`; 429 → retryable `RateLimited`; other 4xx/5xx → non-retryable `ExecutionFailed`; transport failures → retryable `Connection`.
- **Observability**: reuses the server's shared HTTP client so the provider participates in circuit breaking, health checks, and per-provider metrics without extra wiring.
- **Testing**: 37 unit tests including a tiny in-process mock HTTP server that captures request bodies so tests can assert on URL, headers, and JSON payload for every lifecycle branch.

**Server wiring** — `ProviderConfig` gains `opsgenie_*` fields; `main.rs` has a new `"opsgenie"` branch in the provider match.

**Simulation** — `crates/simulation/examples/opsgenie_simulation.rs` walks through `create` → `acknowledge` → `close` plus a rule-based P1-priority reroute. Runs offline with a recording provider.

**Docs** — new `docs/book/features/opsgenie.md` covering TOML config, payload shape, rule integration, outcome body, and error mapping. `docs/design-alertmanager-parity.md` updated with a Phase 4a "Shipped" section.

## Example TOML

```toml
[[providers]]
name = "opsgenie-prod"
type = "opsgenie"
opsgenie_api_key = "ENC[AES256_GCM,data:...]"
opsgenie_region = "us"
opsgenie_default_team = "platform-oncall"
opsgenie_default_priority = "P3"
opsgenie_default_source = "acteon"
```

## Example payload

```json
{
  "event_action": "create",
  "message": "High error rate on checkout-api",
  "alias": "checkout-api-5xx",
  "priority": "P2",
  "tags": ["checkout", "5xx", "slo-breach"],
  "responders": [{"name": "checkout-oncall", "type": "team"}]
}
```

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p acteon-opsgenie --lib` — 37 passing
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins --tests` — full suite green
- [x] `cargo clippy -p acteon-opsgenie -p acteon-server --no-deps --lib --tests -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo run -p acteon-simulation --example opsgenie_simulation` — 3 lifecycle dispatches + reroute assertions pass
- [x] UI lint + build — green

## Remaining Phase 4 providers

VictorOps, Pushover, WeChat, and Telegram are still pending — each will ship as its own PR so a review problem in one cannot block the others.

## Summary
- **COMPILE_ONLY cache save**: Move `COMPILE_ONLY` return after `cache_manager.set()` so pkl is actually persisted to disk. Previously `COMPILE_ONLY=1` returned before saving, making AOT pre-compilation useless.
- **Cross-arch compilation**: Remove address space check in `DLTensorAdaptor.buildMemRefDesc()` to allow CPU tensor tracing. This enables `COMPILE_ONLY=1 ARCH=gfx950` on a gfx942 host (or any machine with LLVM AMDGPU backend).

## Usage
```bash
# AOT compile for gfx942 and gfx950 (CPU tensors, no kernel execution)
COMPILE_ONLY=1 ARCH=gfx942 python aot_compile.py
COMPILE_ONLY=1 ARCH=gfx950 python aot_compile.py

# Deploy: copy ~/.flydsl/cache/ to target machine, kernels load from cache (~28ms vs ~1000ms compile)
```

author: sammygallo
body:
## Summary

Finishes the Phase 8.5 Data Bank / RAG stub. The core pipeline (chunking, embedding, cosine similarity retrieval, upload UI) was already working for solo chats — this PR closes two gaps and runs the first end-to-end smoke test.

### Gap 1: Group chat silently skipped RAG

`buildGroupConversationContext` never accepted a `ragContext` parameter and its caller `generateGroupTurn` never called `resolveRagContext` — so group chat users got zero Data Bank retrieval while the feature appeared to work.

**Fix:** `buildGroupConversationContext` accepts an optional `ragContext` and appends it to the single flat system prompt (group chats use one big system message, not the Phase 9 section-map, so no `promptOrder` fork is needed). `generateGroupTurn` calls `resolveRagContext` scoped to the **current speaker's** avatar — so Seraphina's character-scoped docs only fire on Seraphina's turn, matching how solo chat scopes per-character.

### Gap 2: No source provenance on injected chunks

`resolveRagContext` was joining retrieved chunks with `\n\n---\n\n` and the model saw anonymous blobs. Users couldn't debug which document a passage came from, and the model couldn't cite sources.

**Fix:** `ScoredChunk` (in `embeddings.ts`) gains a `docName` field threaded through `findTopK`'s input/output. `queryRelevantChunks` attaches `docName` from the parent document at flatten time — **no on-disk schema change**: `DocumentChunk` stays `{id, text, embedding}` and the doc name is joined at query time from the parent `DataBankDocument.name`. `resolveRagContext` formats each chunk with `[From: docname]\n${text}`.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/utils/embeddings.ts` | `ScoredChunk` adds `docName`; `findTopK` threads it through input/output |
| `src/stores/dataBankStore.ts` | `queryRelevantChunks` returns `Array<{text, docName}>`; attaches `docName` from parent doc at flatten time |
| `src/stores/chatStore.ts` | (a) `resolveRagContext` formats with `[From: ...]` prefix; (b) `buildGroupConversationContext` accepts+appends `ragContext`; (c) `generateGroupTurn` calls `resolveRagContext` and threads it through |

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc -b` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — clean (tsc + vite, 908 kB bundle)
- [x] `eslint` on all three files — clean
- [x] End-to-end smoke test in live dev preview, stubbing the OpenAI embeddings endpoint with a constant unit vector (`[1/sqrt(1536); 1536]`) so every query matches:
  - [x] Seeded a global `ember_lore` doc + a character-scoped `seraphina_only_lore` doc
  - [x] **Global scope query**: returns only `ember_lore` ✓
  - [x] **Character scope match** (`seraphina.png`): returns both `ember_lore` + `seraphina_only_lore` ✓
  - [x] **Character scope miss** (`doctor.png`): returns only `ember_lore` (seraphina-scoped doc correctly excluded) ✓
  - [x] Verified `resolveRagContext` output format: `[From: ember_lore]\nThe secret password for Ember's vault is CYBERPUNK42. …` ✓
- [x] Grepped production bundle for wiring:
  - `[From: ` appears 1 time (in `resolveRagContext`)
  - `Relevant background information` appears 2 times (in `buildConversationContext` section map AND in `buildGroupConversationContext`'s new finalSystemPrompt)
- [x] Test data + API key cleaned from localStorage before committing
- [ ] Manual: verify with a real OpenAI API key that the full pipeline works end-to-end in both solo and group chats
- [ ] Manual: verify group chat token budget with a large Data Bank doc (known limitation — group chat has no token-aware trimming)

## Known limitations (out of scope — tracked as follow-ups)

- Group chat has no token-aware history trimming (uses `.slice(-30)`), so a very large RAG injection + long history could push shorter-context models over budget
- `queryRelevantChunks` fails silently on API errors (existing behavior preserved)
- No batch embedding optimization — `embedDocument` still makes one API call per chunk in parallel
- No multi-character document linking (a doc can only be global or tied to one character)
- No re-embed on document edit

body:
Login relied on `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` for session state while the server used signed HttpOnly cookies — a split-brain auth model. Password recovery via security questions had working server actions but no UI to invoke them. Bootstrap used wrong env var names (`ADMIN_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD`).

### Auth cleanup (server-side only)

- **`login/page.tsx`**: Removed `getSession()`/`setSession()` from `@/lib/auth`. Session check on mount now hits `/api/auth/session`. After `loginUser()` succeeds, the cookie is already set server-side — just redirect.
- **`auth-guard.tsx`** (both copies): Removed `clearSession()` calls. Guard already validates via `/api/auth/session`; localStorage cleanup was vestigial.
- **`loginUser()`**: Cookie creation failure (missing `SESSION_SECRET`) now returns a hard error instead of `console.warn` + silent pass-through:

```ts
} catch (cookieError) {
  console.error('[auth] Could not set session cookie:', cookieError);
  return {
    success: false,
    error: 'Error de configuración del servidor. Contactá al administrador (SESSION_SECRET no configurada).',
  };
}
```

- **`perfil/page.tsx`**, **`admin/usuarios/page.tsx`**: Switched from `getSession()` (localStorage) to fetching `/api/auth/session` for session data.

### Password recovery page

- New **`/recuperar-contrasena`** page: 3-step flow (email → answer security questions → set new password). Calls existing `getSecurityQuestions()` and `resetPasswordWithQuestions()` server actions.
- Added "¿Olvidaste tu contraseña?" link to login page.
- Added `/recuperar-contrasena` to public routes in middleware and both auth guards.

### Secure bootstrap

- `ADMIN_EMAIL` → `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD` → `ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD`. Both now **required** (removed fallback default email).
- Updated `.env.example`, `README.md`, `docs/auth.md`.

### Already in place (no changes needed)

- Backup routes (`/api/backup/download`, `/api/backup/upload`) already use `requireVerifiedAdmin()`.
- `resetPasswordWithQuestions` already hashes with scrypt and accepts a real new password — no hardcoded password dependency.
- No magic URL rescue endpoints added per requirements.

body:
## What changed
- replaced the `x-research` `.env` loader with a sanitized export flow instead of shell `eval`
- documented that values containing spaces must be quoted to keep `config/.env` shell-compatible
- added a regression test for topic values such as `Claude Code` and `gpt 5.4`

## Why
The failure was caused by shell-incompatible `.env` values, not by the X API itself. Some runners source `config/.env` directly, and lines like `X_TOPICS_ANTHROPIC=...,Claude Code` make the shell try to execute `Code` as a command. That is why the reproduced error was `config/.env: line 31: Code: command not found`.

## Impact
- `x-research` now loads config without executing raw `.env` content
- template and docs steer users toward shell-safe config values
- local secrets remain outside git: `config/.env` is still ignored and was not staged

## Validation
- `sh plugins/x-research/skills/x-research/scripts/tests/run.sh`
- `cd plugins/x-research/skills/x-research && bash -lc '. config/.env'`
- `bash plugins/x-research/skills/x-research/scripts/search.sh --query 'OpenAI Pro tier usage limits' --period week --limit 3`
- `git diff --cached -U0 | rg -n 'xai-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|Authorization: Bearer|API_KEY=.*[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'`

author: aman-cool
body:
Found a spot in the sherdlock selector where we lock a token but then hit a parse error and just... return. Never unlock. The token sits locked in `tokenlockdb` until the lease cleanup goroutine gets around to it (or forever if cleanup is off).

Two lines in `selectInternal`; after `TryLock` succeeds, if `ToQuantity` fails or `sum.Add` fails, we were bailing without calling `UnlockAll`. Every other error path in the same loop does the unlock correctly, these two just got missed.

Added the `UnlockAll` call before each of those returns. That's it.

author: simonwuelker
body:
Previously the code was computing a prefix sum over the number of preceding elements in tree order to get the index that the node should be inserted in.

That's not great if the DOM tree is big. Instead, we can compare two nodes individually by looking at their ancestor chain and then find the correct position with binary search.

On https://262.ecma-international.org/16.0/index.html, this reduces the time it takes for content to appear from around 33s to 16s.

Part of https://github.com/servo/servo/issues/44113

author: chronostasys
body:
## Summary

Fix `TestGrepTool_RemoteSandbox_Basic` hang (also caused Windows CI failure) and add audit logging for Feishu subscription switching.

## Bug 1: MockSandbox infinite loop (all platforms, not just Windows)

`SetDir`, `SetFile`, and `MkdirAll` in `MockSandbox` all had the same bug:

``\go
// BEFORE (broken): compares against original path — never terminates
for p := filepath.Dir(path); p != path && p != "." && p != ""; p = filepath.Dir(p) {

// AFTER (fixed): compares consecutive results — terminates at filesystem root
for p, prev := filepath.Dir(path), path; p != prev; p, prev = filepath.Dir(p), p {
```

The original code compared each `filepath.Dir()` result against the **original** `path` argument (which never changes), so the loop never terminated. The fix compares each result against the **previous** result — `filepath.Dir` returns the same string at filesystem roots (`"/" -> "/"`, `"C:\\\" -> "C:\\\"`), providing a natural termination condition.

## Bug 2: Feishu subscription switch audit log

User reported that switching active subscription caused all subs to display identical fields. DB analysis confirmed `SetDefault` SQL only modifies `is_default` — no data corruption. Added detailed audit logging before subscription activate to capture full state for next reproduction.

- [x] `TestGrepTool_RemoteSandbox_Basic` passes (was hanging before)
- [x] All `./tools/` tests pass with `-race`
- [x] `go build`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` all pass

author: xerpi
body:
The previous fix (a93e009a) changed the inner do-while loop into a
while-at-top loop, checking exit conditions before the first
execution. But those conditions (res, hit_breakpoint, etc.) only
make sense after execution — checking them first caused the loop
to break immediately without executing any guest code (0 fps).

Restore do-while semantics: always execute at least once, then
check the loop condition under the mutex. The to_do read at the
top of each iteration (step vs run decision) and the exit
condition at the bottom are both protected by the mutex.

Also fix suspend() to hold the mutex before modifying to_do,
matching what resume() and exit_delete() already do.

author: skevetter
body:
## Summary

Fixes #127

- Consolidates `pkg/open.Run()`, which detects AppImage environments and sanitizes the process environment before spawning `xdg-open`
- Strips `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `APPDIR`, and other AppImage-injected variables that cause library conflicts for child processes
- Uses `/usr/bin/xdg-open` by absolute path to bypass Tauri's bundled wrapper

### Background

When running inside a Linux AppImage, the `AppRun` script prepends bundled library paths to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Child processes like `xdg-open` and `gio` then load these bundled libraries instead of the system ones, causing symbol lookup errors (e.g. `undefined symbol: g_unix_mount_entry_get_options`). This prevents JetBrains Gateway and other applications from opening via custom URL schemes.

References:
- https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageKit/issues/396
- https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageKit/issues/616
- https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/10617

author: matte-ui
body:
### Motivation
- The existing provider-level Trading 212 connection model limited users to one connection per provider and mixed credentials/sync state at provider scope. The change introduces an account-based model so a single user can link multiple broker accounts with independent credentials and state.
- Credentials must be stored encrypted and never exposed raw in API responses, and all sync/automation state must be scoped per linked account to avoid a broken account blocking others.
- The Broker Control Dashboard UX must surface multiple linked accounts for Trading 212 with per-account actions (sync, edit credentials, automation, disconnect).

### Description
- Data model and migration: refactored Trading 212 config to store per-account records in `user.trading212.accounts` with `id`, `accountLabel`/`label`, `encryptedApiKey`, `encryptedApiSecret`, `connectionStatus`, `syncStatus`, `lastSyncAt`, `automationEnabled`, `providerAccountType`, `providerMetadata`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and `active`, and added migration/normalization in `ensureTrading212Config` to lift legacy single-credential fields into a primary account non-destructively.
- Encryption helpers: added `BROKER_CREDENTIAL_SECRET` handling and helpers `encryptBrokerCredential` / `decryptBrokerCredential` to encrypt API key/secret at rest and decrypt only server-side; responses now return only masked credential placeholders, never raw secrets.
- Backend API: added account-scoped endpoints `GET /api/broker-accounts`, `POST /api/broker-accounts`, `PATCH /api/broker-accounts/:brokerAccountId`, `DELETE /api/broker-accounts/:brokerAccountId`, and `POST /api/broker-accounts/:brokerAccountId/sync` for listing, creating, updating (label/credentials/automation/type), soft-deleting, and triggering sync for individual accounts; retained `/api/integrations/trading212` for compatibility but augmented it to report `brokerAccounts` summaries.
- Sync pipeline and runtime: updated `syncTrading212ForUser` to operate per-account, accept an optional `brokerAccountId` and `force` option, scope sync locks by `t212-sync:${username}`, and track per-account sync state and cooldowns so one account failure does not block others; updated scheduling to respect per-account automation state.
- Frontend/UI: replaced the single-provider broker tile with a multi-account Trading 212 manager (`static/profile-trading-accounts-page.js` + `profile-trading-accounts.html`) allowing viewing linked accounts, adding accounts, per-account edit/credential rotation, per-account sync, per-account automation toggles, and disconnect actions; added compact styling in `static/style.css` consistent with existing design system.
- Safety & UX: editing endpoints preserve existing secret when secret field is omitted; new account responses expose `credentialsMasked` and `hasApiKey`/`hasApiSecret` flags only.

### Testing
- Ran `node --check server.js` and `node --check static/profile-trading-accounts-page.js`, both succeeded (syntax checks passed). 
- Ran full test suite with `npm test -- --test-reporter=spec`, which executed the existing tests; results: 120 tests passed and 2 tests failed (`test/ibkr-connector-heartbeat.test.js` and `test/ibkr-connector-persistence.test.js`) due to an unrelated runtime error reported as `TypeError: z.any is not a function` in the test harness, not caused by the Trading 212 account refactor. 
- Manually exercised account flows via the new endpoints in local DB (create, patch, delete, sync) and verified encrypted storage of credentials and that no raw secrets are returned in responses.

author: seanpor
body:
## Summary
- Root cause of the repeatedly-red \`test-python\` job on main: \`test_backup_directory_writable_validation\` mocks \`os.access\` with equality (\`mode == os.W_OK\`) but prod code calls \`os.access(path, R_OK | W_OK | X_OK)\` — a single call with \`mode == 7\`. Neither equality branch matches, the default \`return True\` falls through, validation passes, and the test hits real Redis at \`localhost:6379\`. Dev boxes run Redis → test silently passes. CI doesn't → \`ConnectionError 111\`.
- Fix: match with bitwise AND (\`mode & os.W_OK\`) and also patch \`pathlib.Path.mkdir\` (Python 3.14 \`mkdir(exist_ok=True)\` now calls \`os.stat\` internally, same gotcha already patched in the sibling tests).
- Documented both failure modes systemically in AGENTS.md so new tests don't repeat the pattern, plus a note that CI runs with \`-x\` and fixes should be validated against the full suite locally before pushing.

author: lboileau
body:
Four new tables to back the activity-ladder feature:
- activity_ladders: ladder metadata + current round/match pointers
- ladder_activities: per-ladder candidates with losses counter + bracket enum
- ladder_participants: the frozen voter snapshot (populated at Start)
- ladder_votes: immutable per-round votes

V040 creates activity_ladders with the three match/winner columns as
plain nullable UUIDs. V041 creates ladder_activities and then adds the
three self-referential FKs to activity_ladders via ALTER TABLE wrapped
in DO $$ EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object blocks for idempotency, since
ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS does not exist in PostgreSQL. V042 and V043
are straightforward.

activity_ladders.creator_id uses ON DELETE CASCADE (not RESTRICT) so
test fixtures that TRUNCATE users CASCADE continue to work, and so
deleting a user cleans up orphaned ladders in production.

All four tables also get schema/tables/*.sql documentation files with

author: lboileau
body:
Fills in every TODO from the client contracts PR with real JDBI and
in-memory logic:

- 15 operations now run real SQL against the V040-V043 tables. Every
  operation exposes its core logic as a companion-object static method
  that takes a JDBI Handle directly (not a Jdbi facade), which is the
  building block for handle-scoped execution inside withLadderLocked.
- 4 row adapters implement RowMapper<T> with snake_case column reads,
  proper enum parsing (valueOf on the enum columns), and correct
  nullable UUID handling via getObject(col, UUID::class.java).
- RestartLadder runs all four mutations (delete votes, delete
  participants, update activities to losses=0/bracket=WINNERS, update
  ladder row to DRAFT/null matches/false flags) inside a single
  jdbi.inTransaction block.
- BulkInsertParticipants uses handle.prepareBatch with ON CONFLICT
  (ladder_id, user_id) DO NOTHING for idempotent atomic inserts.
- AddLadderActivity computes display_order via
  COALESCE((SELECT MAX...), 0) + 1 so the first activity gets 1.
- UpdateLadderStatus sets updated_at = now() on every update and uses
  CAST(:param AS uuid) for nullable UUID binding so null values don't
  trip Postgres type inference.
- CastVote catches the unique (ladder_id, round_number, user_id)
  constraint and returns ConflictError instead of letting the
  SQLException surface as a 500.

withLadderLocked opens a transaction via jdbi.inTransaction, issues
SELECT id FROM activity_ladders WHERE id = :id FOR UPDATE, and on
success passes a HandleScopedActivityLadderClient(handle) to the
caller's block. The scoped client implements the full interface by
calling the same companion methods with the captured handle — every
operation inside the block runs on the same transaction holding the
row lock, guaranteeing exactly-once round resolution. The scoped
client also hoists all 15 validator instances as private vals and
invokes them before executing SQL, so validation behaviour matches
the non-scoped client exactly and won't silently drift as future
validators gain real logic.

FakeActivityLadderClient mirrors the JDBI client's observable
behaviour: same validators, same error types, the same
withLadderLocked semantics (per-ladder synchronized block) with an
upfront ladderStore.containsKey check so a lock call against a
non-existent ladder returns NotFoundError before running the block —
matching the real client and preventing false-pass service tests.

author: lboileau
body:
Fills in every TODO across the activity-ladder service feature: all 8
action bodies, the RoundResolver state machine, ActivityLadderMapper
method bodies, and the vote controller's event-publishing sequence.

Key concurrency points:
- CastVoteAction runs every DB operation that touches vote state
  (castVote, countVotesForRound, getVotesForRound, getActivities,
  updateActivityLossAndBracket, updateLadderState / setLadderWinner)
  inside withLadderLocked via the handle-scoped client. WebSocket
  events are published only after the lock block returns, so the
  broker ack never blocks the lock.
- StartLadderAction also runs inside withLadderLocked. It pre-checks
  status/creator/activities/presentUserIds outside the lock for
  fast-fail, then re-fetches the ladder and activities under the lock
  and re-checks DRAFT status before calling bulkInsertParticipants,
  selecting the first random pair, and updating ladder state. A
  concurrent double-click on Start (two HTTP requests for the same
  DRAFT ladder) correctly serializes on the FOR UPDATE lock; the loser
  sees status=ACTIVE inside the lock and returns 409 Conflict.

RoundResolver implements the full double-elimination state machine
from plan Section 7: tally → tie (no loss change, re-draw pair) or
decided (increment loser's losses, promote to LOSERS/ELIMINATED, check
completion, select next pair). Next-pair selection handles all
bracket-size cases (both ≥2 → random bracket, 1 vs ≥2 → play the
larger, 1 vs 1 → Grand Final). Grand Final Reset is triggered when
the losers-bracket champion wins the first Grand Final; the reset
pairs the same two activities again, and the next resolution
terminates via elimination + LadderCompleted. VoteOutcome.RoundTied
carries isFinalRound and isGrandFinalReset so the controller emits
the correct round-started payload after a tied Grand Final.

RoundResolver reads and writes DB state via the scoped client passed
into resolve(). It is "pure" only in the sense that it has no RNG
state, no WebSocket side effects, and no injected dependencies — it
is deterministic given its inputs and the scoped client. All its
writes happen on the same handle that holds the FOR UPDATE lock.

Controller cast_vote endpoint fans the sealed VoteOutcome into the
right event sequence:
  VoteRecorded   → vote-cast
  RoundTied      → vote-cast + round-resolved(tie) + round-started
  RoundDecided   → vote-cast + round-resolved(decided) + round-started
  LadderCompleted→ vote-cast + round-resolved(decided) + completed

ActivityLadderMapper handles all client ↔ service ↔ DTO conversions.
A toLadderDetailResponse(Ladder) "shell" variant is used by the
restart endpoint (empty activities/participants, frontend refetches)
alongside the full toDetailResponse(LadderDetail) used by every other
read path. ListLaddersAction uses an N+1 lookup for activityCount +
participantCount (per plan Decision 9, MVP).

author: mkhomutov
body:
## Summary

First v0.2 planning RFC. Proposes the **PersonaAgent runtime + three-tier memory system** as the foundational feature that unblocks all other v0.2 work (channels, bridges, sub-agents, protocols, organizations).

### What this RFC covers

1. **PersonaAgent activation** — wire the existing `PersonaAgent` scaffold with autonomous tick loop, event dispatch, and action execution
2. **Three-tier memory** — working memory (context window management), episodic memory (SQLite long-term storage), relationship memory (trust/interaction tracking)
3. **Dynamic persona state** — runtime mood, stress, goal progress injected into LLM prompts
4. **Agent type discrimination** — explicit `type: task | persona` field in `agents.yaml`
5. **Data-driven TaskAgent** — consolidate `CoderAgent`/`ReviewerAgent`/`PlannerAgent` into single YAML-configured class

### v0.2 RFC dependency chain

```
RFC 0005 (PersonaAgent + Memory + TaskAgent)   <- THIS RFC
    |
RFC 0006 (Sub-Agent Spawning)
    |
RFC 0007 (Channels + Bridges)
    |
RFC 0008 (Protocols + Organizations)
```

### Research basis

- Read the full [extension spec](docs/orchestr8-extension-spec.md) (sections E2-E12)
- Cataloged all 45+ TODO stubs across `internal/` and `agents/`
- Reviewed all 38 items in RFC 0004's "Items Deferred to v0.2" section
- Analyzed existing code in `persona.py`, `memory/*.py`, `sub_agents/*.py`

### 6-phase implementation plan

| Phase | Scope | Key Deliverables |
|-------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | Agent type system + TaskAgent | `type` field, `TaskAgent` class, remove 3 agent files |
| 2 | Working memory | `WorkingMemory`, token estimation, priority compression |
| 3 | Episodic memory | SQLite backend, store/recall/summarize |
| 4 | Relationship memory | Trust scores, interaction history, decay |
| 5 | PersonaAgent runtime | Event dispatch, tick loop, action executor |
| 6 | Config validation | `validate.py` implementation, schema updates |

### Open questions (5)

See the RFC for details — key decisions needed on shared vs per-agent SQLite, token estimation approach, and migration strategy for existing agent imports.

body:
Three new routes under /activities:
- /activities — list of all ladders with status badge + counts
- /activities/new — create form with inline add/remove activity rows
  and per-field validation (title non-empty, >=2 activities, each
  activity has a name, an http(s) imageUrl, distanceMinutes >= 0, and
  costPerPerson >= 0 before Submit is enabled)
- /activities/:ladderId — the live ladder page covering every state
  from plan Section 8

The live ladder page subscribes to /topic/ladders/:id over STOMP via
the new useLadderUpdates hook. The hook extends the existing
usePlanUpdates pattern by passing X-User-Id in STOMP CONNECT native
headers so the backend LadderStompSessionListener can record the
subscribing user's presence. deactivate() on unmount lets the backend
decrement the session count cleanly.

ActivityLadderPage handles all 6 plan states: DRAFT creator (editable
activity list + Start button), DRAFT non-creator (read-only +
"waiting for creator"), ACTIVE voter not-yet-voted, ACTIVE voter
already-voted, ACTIVE spectator (clearly labeled), ACTIVE round-
resolved transient (tie/decided banner auto-fades), and COMPLETED
(winner highlighted, Restart button for creator). Every WS event
triggers a refetch of the full ladder detail.

PeoplePanel has two modes:
- DRAFT: a single "In the room" section showing everyone currently
  subscribed to the topic
- ACTIVE / COMPLETED: two sections — "Voters" (the frozen
  ladder.participants list with per-voter online/offline + voted
  indicators) and "Watching" (currently-connected users who are NOT
  in participants). On restart, the panel collapses back to the
  single DRAFT section automatically.

The panel's useUserInfoCache correctly fetches avatars for
participants too: the filter reads "!cache[id] || cache[id].avatar
=== null" so participants that are pre-seeded with username but null
avatar are included in the subsequent getAvatar pass. Previously they
were excluded and all voters rendered as generic silhouettes.

Reuses CamperAvatar's companion AvatarHead (the compact circular
variant already used in the assignments panel), plus the existing
Button, Input, and FormField shared components. No new package.json
dependencies. CSS uses the project's design tokens; no hardcoded
colors.

## Key Changes
* Signal Handling: Added setSignals() and signalHandler() using sigaction() to handle SIGINT and SIGTERM signals.
* Graceful Exit (epoll): Updated the main event loop (Config::run) to run while SignalState::serverRunning is true. Handled errno == EINTR safely across epoll_create, epoll_ctl, and epoll_wait so the server can exit the loop rather than throwing an exception.
* Logging Optimization: Added a LOG_INFO_ON macro toggle in defines.hpp to reduce the application's memory footprint under heavy loads.
* CI/CD Updates: Added a new GitHub Actions step (Run Siege Test with Valgrind) which compiles the server, runs it under Valgrind, blasts it with siege, and sends SIGTERM to verify a leak-free graceful shutdown.
* Cleanup: Removed the unused webserv.hpp header, favoring explicit includes. Included webserv in .gitignore.

author: eloff
body:
### Changelog

None

### Docs

None

### Description

The idea is to have some tests for remote access that actually connect to a local livekit and exercise the remote access bindings in C++.

These tests mirror the rust tests, at least the ones that could be ported. Some that were rust specific were dropped.

We don't have access to the protocol types to deserialize them, so we parse them either as JSON or as binary messages as needed. The binary messages we need to support are quite simple, so this works out.

I tried exporting some functionality from rust for the tests (like the jwt signing) to reduce code duplication, but it actually just complicated the build by requiring an integration test enabled version of the C library (since they used test dependencies on the rust side we don't need and don't want to compile in otherwise.) I dropped that idea. It could maybe work for some things that we compile anyway (like parsing messages) but the use case there was less compelling.

This adds a CI job to run the tests if C or C++ files change. It's very slow, over 20 minutes. I tried various things to make it run faster, but those either didn't work or they broke it. I'm sure it's possible, but I don't want to spend more time on it now. Instead I just made it so you don't have to wait for it to run of succeed in order to merge. We'll see if that's the right call. Running them locally is much better.

author: lboileau
body:
43 JDBI integration tests covering all 16 methods of the
ActivityLadderClient interface against a real PostgreSQL via
Testcontainers. Tests live in
clients/activity-ladder-client/src/test/kotlin/.../JdbiActivityLadderClientTest.kt.

Coverage highlights:
- Every operation has at least one happy-path test.
- Validator integration: distanceMinutes < 0 and costPerPerson < 0
  round-trip through the real ValidateAddLadderActivity.
- NotFoundError pinned down on getLadderById, updateLadderState,
  setLadderWinner, and removeActivity (each verifies the 0-rows-
  affected contract).
- ConflictError pinned down on duplicate castVote for the same
  (ladder_id, round_number, user_id).
- Row-adapter round-trips for every enum value (LadderStatus x3,
  LadderBracket x3), nullable UUID columns (set then cleared), and
  BigDecimal costPerPerson at 42.50 and 0.01.
- restartLadder atomicity tested from both ACTIVE and COMPLETED
  source states. The COMPLETED test seeds via real client calls
  (updateLadderState to ACTIVE then setLadderWinner to COMPLETED)
  so winnerActivityId is set through the real FK-aware path, then
  asserts the full reset including winnerActivityId = null.
- bulkInsertParticipants idempotency: calling twice with overlapping
  user IDs does not raise (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).

The critical concurrency test for withLadderLocked uses a
CyclicBarrier(2) to release two threads simultaneously into the
locked region. Each thread reads the current currentRoundNumber from
the scoped client, records it in a CopyOnWriteArrayList, then writes
current + 1 via updateLadderState. After both threads join the test
asserts currentRoundNumber == 2 (no lost update) AND that the second
thread observed the first thread's commit (readValuesInsideLock
contains exactly {0, 1}). A broken SELECT ... FOR UPDATE would
produce currentRoundNumber == 1 and {0, 0}, failing both assertions.

No mocks. No @Disabled / @Ignore. Tests are independent (@BeforeEach
truncates ladder_votes, ladder_participants, ladder_activities,
activity_ladders, users CASCADE in child-first order). Every test
runs against a real Testcontainers PostgreSQL instance.

Adds declarative, event-driven workflow orchestration (flows) to ClawPilot instances. Flows define multi-agent collaboration as DAGs with parallel execution, mission sessions, and a briefing/SITREP cycle inspired by military doctrine (OPORD/ORBAT).

**Key components:**
- **DB migration v33**: 3 tables (`rt_flow_definitions`, `rt_flow_runs`, `rt_flow_step_runs`)

author: albertogallensf
body:
## Problem

When `AzureProvider` is configured to request tokens scoped to a first-party Microsoft resource (e.g. Dynamics 365 Business Central with scope `https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com/.default`), Azure emits **v1-format tokens**. These tokens differ from v2 tokens in three ways that cause validation to fail:

1. **Issuer** is `https://sts.windows.net/{tid}/` instead of `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tid}/v2.0`
2. **Audience** is `api://{client_id}` instead of the bare `{client_id}` — and when `identifier_uri` is a custom URI (not the default `api://{client_id}`), the `api://{client_id}` format is not in the accepted audience list
3. **Scopes**: the `.default` scope does not appear in the `scp` claim, so if no other non-OIDC scopes are configured, validation raises `ValueError` before even checking the token

Microsoft documents this behaviour: [Access token formats](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/access-tokens#token-formats).

## Solution

### 1. Issuer v1 support

Pass both v2 and v1 issuer URLs as a list to `JWTVerifier` (which already supports `issuer: str | list[str]`):

\`\`\`python
issuer: list[str] = [
    f"https://{base_authority}/{tenant_id}/v2.0",
    f"https://sts.windows.net/{tenant_id}/",
]
\`\`\`

### 2. Audience v1 fallback

Explicitly include `api://{client_id}` alongside `client_id` and `identifier_uri`:

\`\`\`python
audience: list[str] = [client_id, f"api://{client_id}"]
if self.identifier_uri not in audience:
    audience.append(self.identifier_uri)
\`\`\`

This extends the existing fix from #3797 to also cover the case where `identifier_uri` is a custom URI different from `api://{client_id}`.

### 3. Scope validation relaxation

When all requested scopes are OIDC scopes (or the list is empty after filtering), skip scope enforcement instead of raising `ValueError`. The token is still validated by issuer and audience. This is common when the only scope requested from Azure is `<resource>/.default`.

All three fixes applied to both `AzureProvider` and `AzureJWTVerifier`.

## How we discovered this

We are building an MCP server that connects Claude.ai to Dynamics 365 Business Central via FastMCP's `AzureProvider`. The app registration uses `identifier_uri="https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com"` and requests scope `https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com/.default`. Azure returns v1-format tokens that FastMCP rejected on all three counts.

## Changes

- `src/fastmcp/server/auth/providers/azure.py` — issuer as list, audience with `api://` fallback, scope validation relaxation (both classes)
- `tests/server/auth/providers/test_azure.py` — updated issuer/audience assertions
- `tests/server/auth/providers/test_azure_scopes.py` — updated issuer assertions, scope tests now verify enforcement is skipped, added `test_validates_token_with_v1_issuer`

## Test plan

- [x] All 77 Azure provider tests pass (76 existing + 1 new v1 issuer test)
- [x] Multi-tenant configurations (`organizations`, `consumers`, `common`) unaffected — issuer remains `None`
- [x] OBO integration tests unaffected
- [x] Scope enforcement still works for non-OIDC scopes

author: dylan-conway
body:
## What

`Bun.connect({unix})` / `net.createConnection({path})` reported `code: "ENOENT"` for every synchronous `connect(2)` failure on a unix socket, even when the socket file exists and the kernel returned a different error.

Node.js passes the real errno through:

| scenario | kernel errno | Node.js | Bun before | Bun after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| listen backlog full | `EAGAIN` | `EAGAIN` | `ENOENT` | `EAGAIN` |
| file exists, no listener | `ECONNREFUSED` | `ECONNREFUSED` | `ENOENT` | `ECONNREFUSED` |
| file does not exist | `ENOENT` | `ENOENT` | `ENOENT` | `ENOENT` |

## How

`bsd_do_connect_raw` already returns the errno as its return value, but `internal_bsd_create_connect_socket_unix` discarded it (and `close(fd)` could clobber thread-local errno before the caller read it). `Listener.zig` then hard-coded `ENOENT` for any unix-connect failure, and `handleConnectError` flattened whatever it received to `ENOENT`-or-`ECONNREFUSED`.

This threads an `int *err` out-param from `bsd_do_connect_raw`'s return value up through `us_socket_context_connect_unix` → `SocketContext.connectUnix` → `connectUnixAnon` → `doConnect` → `Listener.connectInner`, and changes `handleConnectError` to map the received errno via `SystemErrno` rather than flattening it.

The macOS `saved_errno` dance around the dirfd cleanup in `bsd_create_connect_socket_unix` is removed since `*err` is set before any cleanup syscalls run.

## Test

`test/js/bun/net/unix-connect-backlog-errno.test.ts` creates a raw `AF_UNIX` listener with `listen(fd, 1)` that never `accept()`s, fills the backlog, and asserts the next connect fails with `EAGAIN` (not `ENOENT`). Fails on 1.3.11–1.3.13 without this change.

author: sbriggssjc
body:
## Summary
This change fixes a race condition in the government listings pipeline where listings were not being properly closed when a sale transaction already existed for the property. The issue occurred because the `close_listing_on_sale` trigger fires on sale INSERT, but the pipeline creates the listing AFTER the sale, causing the trigger to find no active listing to close.

## Key Changes
- Added post-insert validation logic to `upsertGovListings()` that checks for recent sales (within 2 years) after creating a new listing
- When a recent sale is found, the newly created listing is immediately closed with:
  - Status set to "Sold"
  - Off-market date set to the sale date
  - Cap rate updated to the sold cap rate (if available)
  - Updated timestamp recorded
- Returns 0 (indicating a sold/inactive listing) instead of 1 when a recent sale is detected
- Maintains backward compatibility by returning 1 for genuinely active listings with no recent sales

## Implementation Details
- Uses a 2-year lookback window to identify relevant sales transactions
- Queries the `sales_transactions` table ordered by most recent sale first
- Only processes the latest sale if multiple sales exist within the window
- Gracefully handles cases where sold cap rate is unavailable (sets to null)

author: alkanen
body:
This pull request introduces a "plan checkpoint" feature to the `/plan` command in the autonomous task orchestrator, enhancing safety and user control. By default, after the initial planning phase, the orchestrator now pauses to display the generated task tree and asks the user to confirm before any execution begins. This checkpoint can be bypassed by providing the `--autonomous` flag, allowing unattended runs. The implementation includes updates to the orchestrator logic, display backends, REPL command handling, documentation, and tests.

**Plan checkpoint and autonomous flag integration:**

- Added a plan checkpoint to the orchestrator's `run()` method: after planning, the user is prompted to review and approve the task tree before execution begins, unless `--autonomous` is specified. The checkpoint is only shown once per run and is reset for each new `/plan` invocation. author: key4ng
body:
## Description

### Problem

[#1034](https://github.com/lightseekorg/smg/pull/1034) added the MlxEngine proto and Rust client. This PR adds the corresponding Python servicer that actually runs mlx-lm on Apple Silicon, completing the end-to-end pipeline.

### Solution

A new `grpc_servicer/smg_grpc_servicer/mlx/` module implementing the `MlxEngine` proto service. Wraps mlx-lm's `BatchGenerator` behind the gRPC contract from PR #1034, enabling SMG to route requests to Apple Silicon workers the same way it routes to vLLM/SGLang/TRT-LLM.

## Changes

### Python servicer (`grpc_servicer/smg_grpc_servicer/mlx/`)
- **`MlxEngineServicer`** — implements all 8 RPCs. Generate supports both streaming and non-streaming. A background daemon thread runs `BatchGenerator.next()` in a tight loop and dispatches tokens to per-request `asyncio.Queue`s via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`.
- **`MlxHealthServicer`** — standard `grpc.health.v1.Health` protocol for liveness/readiness probes.
- **`server.py`** — CLI entrypoint with model loading, warmup, graceful shutdown. Run via `python -m smg_grpc_servicer.mlx.server --model <path>`.

### Sampling parameter mapping

| Proto field | mlx-lm API |
|-------------|-----------|
| `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p` | `make_sampler(...)` |
| `repetition_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `logit_bias` | `make_logits_processors(...)` |
| `max_tokens`, `stop_token_ids`, `ignore_eos` | `BatchGenerator.insert` + `SequenceStateMachine` |
| `logprobs` | Top-k extraction from `generate_step` logprobs array |
| `seed` | `mx.random.seed()` (best-effort, global state) |

### Packaging
- New `mlx` optional dependency in `grpc_servicer/pyproject.toml`: install with `pip install smg-grpc-servicer[mlx]`
- `smg-grpc-proto` Python package exports `mlx_engine_pb2` / `mlx_engine_pb2_grpc`

### E2E test (`e2e_test/chat_completions/test_mlx_backend.py`)

5 tests exercising the full SMG router → gRPC → MLX pipeline:

- basic chat completion
- streaming chat
- tool calling via SMG's qwen `ToolParser` (parses `<tool_call>` tags)
- reasoning content via Qwen3 thinking mode
- `max_tokens` finish reason

Uses `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit` (~400 MB). Skipped on non-Darwin/non-arm64 via module-level `pytestmark`.

Infrastructure additions:
- `Runtime.MLX` enum + `is_mlx()` helper in `e2e_test/infra/constants.py`
- `_build_mlx_cmd()` in `e2e_test/infra/worker.py` (gRPC-only, rejects HTTP mode)
- Model spec entry for `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit`

### CI (`.github/workflows/pr-test-mlx.yml`)

Runs the E2E test on `macos-14` (Apple Silicon) GitHub-hosted runners.

- Triggers only on MLX-related path changes
- Caches Rust target (via `Swatinem/rust-cache`) and HF model (`~/.cache/huggingface/hub`)
- Uses debug maturin build (correctness test, not perf test — saves ~5 min vs release)
- Estimated: first run ~12 min, cached runs ~4-5 min

## Test Plan

Verified locally on Apple Silicon with `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit`: 15/15 test passes across 3 consecutive runs. Also verified earlier with `mlx-community/Qwen3-8B-4bit` for production-quality output.

```bash
# Local run
E2E_RUNTIME=mlx pytest e2e_test/chat_completions/test_mlx_backend.py -v
```

- [x] `cargo +nightly fmt` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] E2E test verified locally
- [ ] (Optional) Documentation updated
- [ ] (Optional) Please join us on Slack [#sig-smg](https://slack.lightseek.org) to discuss, review, and merge PRs

</details>

## Summary
This PR updates the media file saving functionality to save files to the Downloads folder instead of the Pictures/Gallery folder, providing a more appropriate destination for user-downloaded content.

## Key Changes
- **Renamed function**: `saveToGallery()` → `saveToDownloads()` in `MediaFileManager`
- **Updated MediaStore target**: Changed from `MediaStore.Images.Media` to `MediaStore.Downloads`
- **Updated directory path**: Changed from `Environment.DIRECTORY_PICTURES` to `Environment.DIRECTORY_DOWNLOADS`
- **Improved file operations**: Added `IS_PENDING` flag to MediaStore entry for atomic writes (API 29+)
- **Enhanced error handling**: Added try-catch block with cleanup (delete pending entry on failure)
- **Updated UI references**: Updated all function calls and user-facing messages throughout the codebase
  - `saveImageToGallery()` → `saveImageToDownloads()` in `ChatViewModel`
  - Updated snackbar message from "Saved to gallery" → "Saved to Downloads"
  - Updated composable parameter and descriptions in `FullscreenImageViewer`
  - Updated temporary file naming from `gallery_*` → `download_*`

## Implementation Details
- The `IS_PENDING` flag ensures the file is not visible to other apps until the write operation completes successfully
- Added proper cleanup: if the write fails, the pending MediaStore entry is deleted before re-throwing the exception
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with the existing API surface while improving the user experience

body:
## Summary

This PR completes the `v81-v86` adoption-and-contract cleanup after the quality-weighted consensus promotion.

It does three things:

- adds a structured `monthly_summary.json` artifact to the monthly output bundle
- updates the email/dashboard/workflow surfaces to use the current live artifact contract
- retires the equal-weight consensus from the primary operator-facing report and email while keeping `consensus_shadow.csv` for diagnostics

## What Changed

- added `src/reporting/monthly_summary.py` and now write `results/monthly_decisions/<YYYY-MM>/monthly_summary.json`
- added `src/reporting/dashboard_snapshot.py` and now commit a static monthly `dashboard.html` snapshot
- updated `scripts/monthly_decision.py` to write the new artifacts and stop rendering the visible `Consensus Shadow Evaluation` section in the main recommendation memo
- updated `src/reporting/email_sender.py` to support the new summary payload and current dashboard snapshot linking
- updated `dashboard/app.py` and `dashboard/data.py` to consume the newer artifact bundle directly instead of relying as heavily on markdown parsing
- tightened `.github/workflows/monthly_decision.yml` verification to include `benchmark_quality.csv`, `consensus_shadow.csv`, `dashboard.html`, and `monthly_summary.json`
- refreshed current-state docs to reflect the live `v86` baseline and the new artifact/reporting contract
- regenerated the April 2026 monthly artifact bundle to match the new contract

## Why

The repo had working but partially disconnected operator surfaces:

- the dashboard existed but was not fully integrated into the monthly output contract
- the email renderer had drifted from the live report structure
- the workflow verification step was weaker than the actual artifact surface
- downstream consumers still had to scrape markdown for top-level state

This PR turns the current promoted workflow into a more stable product surface and makes future automation easier.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests\test_workflow_contracts.py tests\test_v65_p26_p27_p28.py tests\test_email_sender_current_report.py tests\test_dashboard_data.py tests\test_dashboard_snapshot.py tests\test_monthly_summary.py tests\test_monthly_pipeline_e2e.py tests\test_monthly_logging.py -v`
- `python -m mypy src\reporting\monthly_summary.py src\reporting\dashboard_snapshot.py dashboard\data.py`
- `python scripts\monthly_decision.py --as-of 2026-04-11 --dry-run --skip-fred`

## Notes

- `data/pgr_financials.db` was intentionally left out of this PR
- `consensus_shadow.csv` remains in the monthly bundle for diagnostic/governance use, but it is no longer a primary recommendation surface

## Summary

Six edits to `docs/design/hybrid-retrieval-multilingual.md` that capture the substantive finding surfaced during PR #246 rounds 3–5: **pgroonga's documented integration is its own PostgreSQL index access method, not the standard `regconfig` registry the Layer 1 design assumes.** Verified via context7 against pgroonga's official documentation.

The follow-up now gates the Layer 1 PG17 verification task on a new Step 0 (\"does pgroonga even register the assumed regconfigs in `pg_ts_config`?\"), defers extension selection to a new Phase 1.05 in the wiring PR, and documents three explicit options with tradeoffs (per-language parser extensions, pgroonga with branched query path, deferral from Layer 1).

**Tracked as #249.** #248 (Postgres memory cost) is now blocked on #249 because there's no point measuring the cost of regconfigs that may not exist.

This is a direct follow-up to the design-doc-edits queue that was assembled during #246's QA cycle but deliberately held until #246 merged, to keep the foundation PR's scope clean.

## Changes

- **Edit 1:** New \"pgroonga regconfig integration is unverified\" subsection added before the existing schema verification task — establishes the framing and cites the context7 verification that surfaced the finding
- **Edit 2:** Schema verification task (Substantive 2) replaced with a gated version: Step 0 (does pgroonga register regconfigs?), Step 1 (basic schema verification — only meaningful if Step 0 succeeds or an alternative is in place), Step 2 (memory measurement, incorporates #248), Step 3 (managed Postgres compatibility), plus the pre-existing trigger-based fallback
- **Edit 3:** \"Via pgroonga extension\" language-support subsection replaced with \"Non-Western language support — extension choice is OPEN\" — includes the three-option trilemma table and the verified zhparser counter-example for the per-language parser approach
- **Edit 4:** Phase 1.0 reference updated to reflect both Substantive 2 and the new Substantive 3
- **Edit 5:** Phase 1.05 (Extension selection) inserted between Phase 1.0 and the schema migration step
- **Edit 6 (audit):** Phase 3 section reframed to cover all three Phase 1.05 options; risk section renamed from \"pgroonga — Low\" to \"Non-Western FTS extension — Low-Medium\" with per-option risk breakdown; managed-Postgres compatibility section reframed to note that neither pgroonga nor zhparser is available on RDS/Aurora/Cloud SQL/Azure; zhparser added to the references list
- **CHANGELOG:** `### Changed` entry under `[Unreleased]` summarizing the above and linking #246/#248/#249

## References

- **#246** — Layer 1 foundation PR where the finding surfaced (merged 2026-04-11)
- **#247** — lingua latency mitigation (independent, not impacted)
- **#248** — Postgres memory cost measurement (BLOCKED on #249)
- **#249** — pgroonga regconfig verification (the blocker this edit documents the plan for)

None. Pure documentation PR. No Python code, tests, dependencies, or build artifacts change. CI still runs ruff/mypy/pytest for the usual safety net — expected to pass unchanged.

### Manual tests

author: pleasedodisturb
body:
## Summary

This PR implements two scoring enhancements for job applications:

1. **Rule-based red flag detection** (#73) — detects problematic signals in job postings without any AI cost
2. **Letter-grade scoring** (#71) — maps 0-10 fit scores to letter grades (A through F) for intuitive readability

## Key Changes

### Backend Red Flag Detection
- New `src/career_os/services/red_flags.py` module with 7 independent detection rules:
  - **stale_posting**: Flags postings older than 60 days
  - **unrealistic_requirements**: Detects 10+ years paired with junior titles or >15 distinct skill tokens
  - **turnover_language**: Identifies high-intensity culture signals without work-life balance mentions
  - **missing_salary**: Enforces salary transparency in mandated jurisdictions (CO, CA, WA, NY, CT)
  - **staffing_agency**: Detects contract-to-hire and staffing agency roles
  - **vague_responsibilities**: Flags short descriptions or excessive generic phrases
  - **excessive_requirements**: Warns on >15 distinct technical skills required
- Each rule returns a flag dict with `flag_type`, `severity` (info/caution/warning/dealbreaker), and `description`
- Comprehensive test coverage in `tests/test_red_flags.py`

### Letter-Grade Scoring
- New `score_to_letter_grade()` function in `src/career_os/schemas/scoring.py` mapping 0-10 scores to A/A-/B+/B/C+/C/D/F
- Added `letter_grade` field to `ScoreResponse` with automatic computation via Pydantic validator
- Mirrored implementation in frontend `lib/gradeUtils.ts` for client-side consistency
- Test coverage in `tests/test_letter_grades.py`

### Frontend Components
- **GradeBadge** component: Displays letter grade + numeric score in a colored pill badge
- **RedFlagBadge** component: Two render modes:
  - Compact: Single warning icon + count pill, colored by worst severity
  - Expanded: Stacked list of severity icon + description rows
- Integrated both components into `ApplicationDetail` and `Discovery` pages
- Updated `KanbanCard` to use new `GradeBadge` instead of inline score display
- Comprehensive component tests in `frontend/src/__tests__/`

### Database & API
- New Alembic migration adding columns to `scored_jobs` table:
  - `red_flags` (JSON array)
  - `ats_keywords` (JSON array, for future use)
  - 6 dimensional sub-score columns (for future use)
- Updated `ScoredJob` model to persist red flags
- Updated `ScoreResponse` schema with `RedFlag` type definition
- Integration in `score_job()` service to detect and persist red flags

### Type Definitions
- Added `RedFlag` and `RedFlagSeverity` types to frontend `api/types.ts`
- Added `RedFlag` Pydantic model to backend schemas

## Implementation Details

- Red flag detection is rule-based and deterministic — no AI calls required
- Rules are independent; failures in one never affect others
- Severity scale provides nuanced signaling: info < caution < warning < dealbreaker
- Letter-grade boundaries are inclusive on the lower bound (e.g., 9.0-10.0 → A)
- Frontend and backend grade-mapping logic kept in sync via mirrored implementations
- All new code includes docstrings and comprehensive test coverage

This implements the user request to provide a small tuning pass on the best picks pipeline, aiming to make Actionable smaller and stronger by utilizing `consensus_agreement` explicitly. 

New rules in `build_best_picks_df`:
- **Side Probability Floor:** Added `SIDE_MIN_WIN_PROB` of 0.50. Sides below this are downgraded to `Below Threshold`.
- **Neutral Overlay:** When `consensus_agreement` is `Neutral`, it requires higher `min_ev` (0.03) and `min_edge` (0.04) and `min_prob` (0.58). Fails drop to `Below Threshold`.
- **Disagrees Overlay:** When `consensus_agreement` is `Disagrees`, it requires even stricter thresholds (0.04 EV, 0.05 Edge, 0.60 prob). Fails drop to `High Variance/Speculative`.
- Added new diagnostics arrays and added rendering for them to `streamlit_app.py`.
- Added tests in `test_actionable_tuning.py` to cover these new constraints securely.

author: fpelliccioni
body:
## Summary

- Migrate `kth::domain::message::get_headers` to the const/mut typed-handle pattern used by the chain classes since 0.79.0.
- `get_headers` inherits from `get_blocks`, so every accessor/serializer inherited from the base is now exposed on the derived binding as well.
- The class lives in `kth::domain::message` but the C-API keeps it under the `chain/` group to preserve the existing `kth_chain_get_headers_*` names.

## What changed in the API

- `kth_get_headers_t` / `kth_get_headers_ptr_t` → `kth_get_headers_mut_t` / `kth_get_headers_const_t`. The `_ptr_t` was referenced only by the (commented-out) `kth_block_locator_fetch_handler_t` callback; that typedef now takes the new `_mut_t` handle.
- `start_hashes()` now returns a borrowed `kth_hash_list_const_t` view (the parent retains ownership) instead of a fresh mutable handle.
- `stop_hash()` returns `kth_hash_t` by value; the old `_out` variant is dropped.
- New functions now exposed:
  - `construct_from_data` (error-code + out-param)
  - `construct_unsafe` (raw `uint8_t*` stop hash variant)
  - `copy` / `equals`
  - `to_data` (wire-format serialization)
  - `set_stop_hash_unsafe` (raw `uint8_t*` variant)

## Test plan

- [x] Catch2 unit tests in `src/c-api/test/chain/get_headers.cpp` cover every function (including those inherited from `get_blocks`) and every `KTH_PRECONDITION` via fork-based death tests.
- [x] `to_data` / `construct_from_data` round-trip verified against `serialized_size`.
- [x] `copy`, `equals`, safe/unsafe constructor parity.
- [x] `kth_capi_test` green on the maintainer's local build.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes the public C-API/ABI for `get_headers` (new handle typedefs and altered getter semantics), which can break downstream bindings despite being mostly mechanical refactoring with added tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refactors the C-API binding for `kth::domain::message::get_headers` to the project’s **const/mut typed-handle** pattern, replacing the legacy `kth_get_headers_t`/`_ptr_t` typedefs and updating the related callback typedef.
> 
> Expands and hardens the `kth_chain_get_headers_*` surface: adds `construct_from_data`, `to_data`, `copy`, `equals`, and safe/unsafe stop-hash setters/constructors; changes `start_hashes` to return a **borrowed const view** and `stop_hash` to return by value (removing the `_out` pattern). Adds comprehensive Catch2 tests and wires them into `kth_capi_test`.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 0fbb490d1c4acd449944e6fbe54fcd8711fc6ca9. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: kinjikawaguchi
body: ## Why Issue #8: `from .module import *` 配下の名前が一切解決されず、wildcard re-export に依存するパッケージで shortening が一切機能しない false-negative が出ていた（README / CLAUDE.md にも既知制約として明記済み）。 ## What `ReexportResolver` がワイルドカード import を再帰的に辿って公開名を収集するよう拡張した。 - `from .x import *` / `from ..x import *` / `from pkg.x import *` を解決 - ターゲットの `__all__` を尊重（存在する場合）、無ければ `_` 始まりの名前を除外（Python のワイルドカード挙動に一致） - `frozenset[str]` の `visited` で循環 wildcard を防御（`pkg → a → pkg` でも停止） - モジュール探索を `__init__.py` と `.py` ファイル両方に対応させ、wildcard ターゲットが通常モジュールでも top-level 定義を拾えるようにした - ネストした wildcard チェーン (`pkg/__init__` → `sub/__init__` → `x.py`) を推移的に解決 ## Test plan - [x] `uv run pytest --cov=minport` — 124 passed, 100% coverage - [x] `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` — clean - [x] `uv run ruff format src/ tests/` — applied - [x] `uv run ty check src/` — clean - [x] `uv run pip-audit` — no vulnerabilities - [x] Issue #8 検証: 新規 R-13〜R-18 が修正前に fail することを確認してから実装 - [x] R-12 を "検出しない (スコープ外)" → "再帰的に解決" へ反転 ## Notes - 検出レイヤー（`_resolve_exports`）でも `_`-prefix フィルタを適用している。これは従来 `from ._priv import X` を wildcard 経由で露出させないためで、純粋な名前空間バインド意味論からは若干厳しいが、PEP 8 の "underscore = private" 慣習に沿う安全側の挙動。 - `_find_module_file` を `__init__.py` / `.py` 両対応に変更。これによりパッケージ候補の探索意味論は変わらないが、wildcard 再帰時にモジュール本体を読めるようになった。 - 閾値コメント・更新履歴コメントは入れていない（CLAUDE.md ルール準拠）。 Closes #8 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---
