## Problem Statement

`StuckConsumerRepairStats` has 3 Tehuti OccurrenceRate sensors for the stuck consumer detection and repair lifecycle but no OTel counterparts, making these metrics unavailable in OTel-based monitoring dashboards.

## Solution

Add 3 OTel COUNTER metrics under the `ingestion.pubsub.consumer.stuck.*` namespace using the joint Tehuti+OTel API (`MetricEntityStateBase`):

- `ingestion.pubsub.consumer.stuck.detected_count` — scans that detected a stuck PubSub consumer
- `ingestion.pubsub.consumer.stuck.task_repaired_count` — ingestion tasks killed to unblock a stuck consumer
- `ingestion.pubsub.consumer.stuck.unresolved_count` — stuck consumers found with no fixable task identified

This is a singleton stats class with `CLUSTER_NAME` as the only dimension. `clusterName` was added to the constructor, passed from `AggKafkaConsumerService` via `serverConfig.getClusterName()`.

author: johanrd
body:
Restores the autofix that [ember-template-lint](https://github.com/ember-template-lint/ember-template-lint/blob/f43c6f11fdf8fc8ecb51ba04cea0f367b1af544b/lib/rules/no-redundant-fn.js) has but was lost during the rule's extraction.

### Behavior
Strips redundant `fn` wrappers around a single path:
```hbs
{{fn this.handleClick}}              →  {{this.handleClick}}        (MustacheStatement)
(fn this.handleClick)                →  this.handleClick            (SubExpression)
```

### Implementation
Uses `fixer.replaceTextRange(node.range, ...)` instead of upstream's AST mutation. For `MustacheStatement`, the replacement wraps in `{{...}}` since the node range includes the curlies; for `SubExpression`, the bare path is used since the range includes the parens.

The existing `isFnShadowed()` check is preserved so that `import { fn } from './my-utils'` in a `.gjs`/`.gts` file is not flagged.

### Test plan
- 25/25 tests pass
- All three upstream test cases mirrored in the HBS suite (SubExpression in modifier, MustacheStatement in component arg, SubExpression in hash pair)
- GTS suite mirrors the same cases inside `<template>...</template>`
- No test cases added or removed beyond filling in `output:` strings

### Reference
- [`no-redundant-fn.js`](https://github.com/ember-template-lint/ember-template-lint/blob/f43c6f11fdf8fc8ecb51ba04cea0f367b1af544b/lib/rules/no-redundant-fn.js)

author: rsned
body:
## Summary
- On a fresh clone, `make run` fails with hundreds of parse errors because the `.godot/` import cache doesn't exist yet. Without it, `class_name` types (`ThemeColors`, `Log`, etc.) aren't registered and resource imports (fonts) fail.
- Adds an `import` Makefile target that runs `godot --headless --import` when `.godot/` is missing
- Makes the `run` target depend on `import` so the first `make run` just works

## Context
The `make run` target launches Godot directly without running the import step first. Godot needs to run its import/editor scan (`$GODOT --headless --import`) to build the `.godot/` cache, which:
- Registers all `class_name` types (`ThemeColors`, `Log`, etc.)
- Imports all resources (fonts, textures, etc.)

Without this step, every script referencing those types fails to parse. The import only runs when `.godot/` is missing, so it adds no overhead on subsequent launches. A full reimport can be forced with `rm -rf .godot && make import`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Clone fresh (or `rm -rf .godot`) and run `make run` — should import automatically then launch cleanly
- [ ] Run `make run` again — should skip import and launch immediately
- [ ] `make import` works standalone

author: mcrundo
body:
## Summary

Three robustness fixes uncovered while testing the picker flow shipped in #1. All fix the same general failure mode: a single LLM slip used to wipe out an entire stage; now stages either recover gracefully or warn loudly.

## Bug fixes

### Map and plan stages: tolerate stray LLM fields

`extra="forbid"` on the chapter-extraction and plan-proposal schemas means a single unknown key from the model used to crash the whole stage. Real failure caught on *The Pragmatic Programmer*: the LLM put `source_quote` on a `Principle` (reasonable generalization from `Concept`, where that field exists) and killed `ch19` mid-map. Plan stage was just as exposed but with worse blast radius — it's one big LLM call, so a single stray field would wipe out the entire plan.

The fix is a new shared helper `validate_with_extra_recovery` in `src/franklin/llm/validation.py`:

- The outgoing tool schema stays strict (`additionalProperties: false`) so the model is still nudged to stay on contract.
- On validation, if the *only* errors are `extra_forbidden`, walk each error's `loc` tuple, strip just those keys from a deep copy of the payload, log a warning naming what was dropped, and retry.
- Any non-extra error (missing required field, wrong type) still raises — recovery is scoped to extras only, we don't mask real bugs.

Mapper and planner both use the shared helper now.

### Reduce stage: warn on unresolved feeds

`generate_artifact` now logs a warning when `ResolvedContext.unresolved` is non-empty, naming the missing path(s) and the artifact path. Previously the resolver collected unresolved feeds into a list that was never read, shipping a degraded artifact without surfacing the missing context.

This became a bigger concern after #1: Gate 1 lets users deselect chapters, and the planner might still propose artifacts that feed from chapters the user removed. The reducer would silently produce a worse file. Now you'll see the warning in the run output.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 378 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` clean
- [x] `uv run mypy` clean
- [ ] Manual: re-run *The Pragmatic Programmer* book that previously hit the `source_quote` validation error — should now complete with a warning logged for the stripped field

New tests (5):

- `test_extract_chapter_recovers_from_stray_extra_field` — single extra recovered, log line emitted
- `test_extract_chapter_recovers_from_multiple_stray_extras` — multi-item extras
- `test_extract_chapter_still_rejects_non_extra_errors` — missing-required-field still raises
- `test_design_plan_recovers_from_stray_extra_field` — planner recovery, mirrors mapper test
- `test_generate_artifact_warns_on_unresolved_feeds` — reducer warning surfaces both paths

author: danielharley
body:
## Summary

This branch adds a persisted PCA/KMeans analysis stage on top of the existing SWeeP embedding snapshot workflow. It introduces a new notebook-driven step that consumes frozen embedding and metadata snapshots, selects clustering parameters from a PCA/KMeans stability grid, and materializes the result as a reusable snapshot artifact.

It also extends the pipeline's persistence and reuse semantics so PCA coordinates, explained variance ratios, cluster assignments, stability-grid output, alignment metadata, and profiling data are saved with manifest-backed provenance. The new flow enforces one-to-one alignment between SWeeP rows and metadata rows via `protein_uid` and supports `create_new`, `reuse_latest`, and `reuse_latest_or_create` snapshot resolution.

## What changed

- add `src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans.py` with reusable helpers for:
  - PCA projection
  - sampled silhouette scoring
  - pairwise ARI statistics across repeated KMeans initializations
  - pairwise ARI statistics across clustering runs on subsamples
  - PCA/KMeans stability-grid generation
  - `(m, k)` selection from stability metrics and silhouette scores
- add `src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans_snapshot.py` to:
  - load upstream SWeeP embedding snapshots and metadata snapshots
  - extract `protein_uid` from `sequence_metadata.record_id`
  - align sequence metadata and NCBI metadata with `validate="one_to_one"`
  - reject missing or duplicate UID mappings before PCA/KMeans materialization
  - save immutable PCA/KMeans snapshots and publish `latest/`
  - load and validate saved PCA/KMeans snapshots for reuse
  - persist manifest-backed artifact hashes, provenance, alignment summaries, parameter-search configuration, selected `(m, k)`, and profiling output
- persist PCA/KMeans snapshot artifacts including:
  - PCA coordinate matrix as `.npy`
  - explained variance ratio vector as `.npy`
  - `cluster_assignments.csv`
  - `stability_grid.csv`
  - `profiling_log.csv`
  - `alignment_report.json`
  - `manifest.json`
- create `notebooks/06_pca_kmeans_analysis.ipynb` to configure the new analysis stage, resolve the upstream snapshots, materialize or reuse the PCA/KMeans snapshot, and preview selected configuration and cluster outputs
- add `scikit-learn` to `requirements.txt` for `PCA`, `KMeans`, `silhouette_score`, and `adjusted_rand_score`
- load the metadata CSV in `src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans_snapshot.py` with `low_memory=False` to avoid mixed-type `DtypeWarning` during snapshot creation

## Why

Before this branch, the pipeline stopped at frozen SWeeP embeddings and did not treat PCA projection, clustering, parameter selection, and cluster-assignment persistence as a first-class reusable workflow.

This branch now guarantees that:
- PCA/KMeans analysis is materialized as its own persisted snapshot type
- selected clustering parameters are derived from an explicit stability grid rather than ad hoc notebook state
- downstream analysis can reuse frozen PCA/KMeans artifacts without recomputing the full workflow
- SWeeP rows and metadata rows must match by exact one-to-one `protein_uid` alignment before clustering proceeds

## Notable implementation details

- the PCA/KMeans selection flow combines sampled silhouette with minimum ARI thresholds across both repeated initializations and repeated subsamples
- if no `(m, k)` combination passes the configured ARI thresholds, selection falls back to a composite score derived from silhouette and clipped minimum ARI values
- metadata alignment depends on parsing `protein_uid` from the structured FASTA-derived `record_id` string in SWeeP sequence metadata
- PCA/KMeans snapshot loading validates artifact type, required files, and saved SHA-256 hashes before reuse
- immutable snapshot directories are created under `snapshots/` and incomplete directories are cleaned up if snapshot creation fails before publication
- `latest/` publication follows the existing repository snapshot replacement semantics rather than writing analysis outputs only to notebook-local state

## Files changed

- `notebooks/06_pca_kmeans_analysis.ipynb`
- `requirements.txt`
- `src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans.py`
- `src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans_snapshot.py`

## Test plan

- Executed verification:
  - run `py -3 -m py_compile "src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans.py" "src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans_snapshot.py"`
  - validate that `notebooks/06_pca_kmeans_analysis.ipynb` deserializes as valid notebook JSON
  - run `py -3 -m py_compile "src/pago_pipeline/pca_kmeans_snapshot.py"` after the metadata CSV read adjustment
- Additional validation plan:
  - run `notebooks/06_pca_kmeans_analysis.ipynb` in the project Python environment after the upstream metadata and SWeeP snapshots exist
  - confirm that the PCA/KMeans step writes `manifest.json`, PCA coordinate `.npy`, explained variance ratio `.npy`, `cluster_assignments.csv`, `stability_grid.csv`, `profiling_log.csv`, and `alignment_report.json`
  - rerun the notebook with `PCA_KMEANS_SNAPSHOT_MODE = SnapshotMode.reuse_latest` and confirm the latest PCA/KMeans snapshot loads successfully
  - verify that the flow rejects upstream inputs when `protein_uid` extraction fails, duplicate UIDs are present, or aligned metadata rows are missing

## Risks / review focus

- `protein_uid` extraction currently assumes the SWeeP `record_id` format continues to encode `protein_uid=<value>` in the FASTA-derived header
- PCA/KMeans snapshot creation now requires complete metadata alignment for every embedding row and will fail if upstream snapshot contents drift out of sync
- the metadata CSV is intentionally loaded with `low_memory=False` to suppress mixed-type inference warnings, which changes pandas parsing behavior for that large heterogeneous file
- end-to-end notebook execution was not evidenced in the CL

body: ## Summary Security audit and hardening of the Guardian Bell MK1 firmware. This PR addresses critical, high, and medium severity security issues found during a comprehensive codebase scan. ### Changes **CRITICAL — TLS Certificate Validation (6 occurrences fixed)** - Replaced all `setInsecure()` calls with ESP-IDF CA certificate bundle (`setCACertBundle(esp_crt_bundle_attach)`) across OTA (`ota.cpp`), Telegram (`telegram.cpp`), and Cloudinary (`cloudinary.cpp`) connections - This prevents man-in-the-middle attacks on all HTTPS connections — especially critical for OTA firmware updates where an attacker could push malicious firmware **CRITICAL — MQTT TLS Encryption** - Upgraded MQTT from plain `WiFiClient` to `WiFiClientSecure` with CA cert bundle validation (`mqtt.cpp`, `mqtt.h`) - MQTT credentials were previously sent in cleartext over port 1883 - Updated `secrets_example.cpp` to recommend port 8883 (TLS) instead of 1883 **HIGH — Information Disclosure Fix** - Replaced 3 unconditional `Serial.printf()` calls in `capture_save_image.cpp` with `DBG_PRINTLN()` macros - These were leaking file paths to serial output even when `SERIAL_DEBUG` was disabled (set to 0), inconsistent with all other debug output in the codebase **MEDIUM — Bug Fix** - Fixed `shouldRing = true` → `shouldDelete = true` in `wipe_sd_card.cpp` debug mode path — the SD card wipe function was referencing an undefined variable ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify TLS connections work on actual hardware** — the ESP-IDF cert bundle adds ~64KB to flash. Confirm the firmware still fits within the OTA partition scheme defined in `partitions/default_ota.csv`. If flash is too tight, consider using `CONFIG_MBEDTLS_CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE_DEFAULT_CMN` (common CAs only) instead of the full bundle. - [ ] **Test MQTT connectivity** — the MQTT client now uses `WiFiClientSecure`. Your MQTT broker (Home Assistant) must support TLS on the configured port. If your broker only supports unencrypted MQTT (port 1883), you'll need to either enable TLS on the broker or revert the MQTT change. - [ ] **Test OTA firmware update flow** — verify that OTA checks and firmware downloads still succeed with certificate validation enabled against your GitHub Releases URL. - [ ] **Test Telegram notifications** — confirm both text messages (`sendMsgToTelegram`) and image uploads (`sendImageToTelegram`) work with the cert bundle. - [ ] **Test Cloudinary uploads** — verify image uploads succeed during the overnight upload window. ### Notes **Remaining issues not fixed in this PR (lower severity / design decisions):** - OTA version comparison uses simple string equality — no semantic versioning or downgrade protection - Hardcoded MQTT client ID `"smart-doorbell"` — would cause connection bouncing with multiple devices - `FLASH_LED_PIN` and `WAKE_PIN` both map to GPIO 4 in `pins.h` — potential hardware conflict - Telegram bot token appears in URL query strings (inherent to the Telegram Bot API design) Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3267a3e7a5044fc4b9e632c298316301 Requested by: @ameenahmedbaig ---

author: bageus
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a non-intrusive visual uplift (Balanced Next‑Gen style) by adding layered VFX and graceful fallbacks without touching core gameplay logic. 
- Improve object readability and tunnel believability by accounting for tube curvature/center offsets and adding soft volumetric slices. 
- Add lightweight, generated asset fallbacks so new visuals work on low-budget targets (Web/Telegram) immediately.

### Description

- Added a new docs file `docs/phaser-visual-max-options-2026-04-10-ru.md` describing visual upgrade options, asset prompts and rollout roadmap. 
- Introduced `js/phaser/entities/entity-visual-assets.js` which exports `VISUAL_UPGRADE_TEXTURES` and `ensureVisualUpgradeTextures`, and generates canvas fallbacks for `shadow_contact_ellipse_01`, `bonus_aura_soft_01`, `coin_glint_star_01`, and `shock_ring_impact_01`. 
- Updated `EntityRenderer` to preload and ensure visual upgrade textures, create/destroy pools for bonus aura and coin glint sprites, apply lane-based micro-rotation/scale to the player sprite, and use generated shadow texture when available. 
- Enhanced projection math in `projectLane` and `projectPolar` to consider `tube.curveAngle`, `centerOffsetX/Y` and compute a `curveOcclusion` factor used to fade/skip objects occluded by tight turns. 
- Extended `renderObjectsPass` to allocate and draw bonus aura and coin glint sprites (with texture or procedural fallback), modulate alphas by `curveOcclusion`, and skip heavily occluded items. 
- Tweaked `renderCollectAnimationsPass` to use the impact texture when present, increase ripple scale/duration, and keep a particle-safe fallback. 
- Modified `tunnel-draw-pass` to incorporate curve offsets into segment geometry, factor `curveOcclusion` into tile alpha, and added `renderVolumetricSlices` to draw soft volumetric slice rings inside the tunnel. 
- UI tweaks in `js/screens.js`: added `setEyesVisibility` and hide/show menu/start transition eye elements when switching screens, and remove `start-transition-active` on gameplay start.

### Testing

- Ran project linters and static checks via `npm run lint` which passed with no errors. 
- Performed a local dev smoke run via `npm run dev` and verified there are no runtime exceptions during scene preload/create and basic gameplay flow (menu → gameplay → game-over). 
- Manually exercised transitions that rely on generated textures (shadow, aura, glint, shock ring) and confirmed fallback canvas textures are created and rendered successfully.
